PV + PVC + Pod — Complete Exam Skeleton

This 3-part pattern is the most tested storage question on the CKA. Write it from memory.

# 1. PersistentVolume (admin creates)
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: my-pv                       # cluster-scoped, no namespace
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 10Gi                    # ◀── total capacity
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce                    # ◀── RWO / ROX / RWX
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain  # ◀── Retain / Delete
  storageClassName: manual           # ◀── must match PVC
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/data                  # ◀── node path (exam default)
---
# 2. PersistentVolumeClaim (developer creates)
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: my-pvc                      # namespaced
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce                    # ◀── must match PV
  storageClassName: manual           # ◀── must match PV
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi                   # ◀── ≤ PV capacity
---
# 3. Pod using PVC
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: my-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    volumeMounts:
    - name: data-vol
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: data-vol
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: my-pvc              # ◀── reference PVC by name

Find PV/PVC YAML Fields Fast

kubectl explain pv.spec                        # PV spec fields
kubectl explain pv.spec.capacity               # storage size
kubectl explain pv.spec.accessModes            # RWO/ROX/RWX
kubectl explain pv.spec.persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy  # reclaim policy
kubectl explain pvc.spec                       # PVC spec fields
kubectl explain pvc.spec.resources.requests    # request size
🔧Admin creates PV
→
👨‍💻Dev creates PVC
→
🔗K8s binds PVC→PV
→
📦Pod mounts PVC
→
✅Data persists!
3 Access Modes (RWO/ROX/RWX)
2 Reclaim Policies (Retain/Delete)
4 PV Statuses
1:1 PV↔PVC Binding

22.1 The PV/PVC Model — Separation of Concerns

Kubernetes storage uses a two-layer model to separate the "how" from the "what". The cluster admin provisions storage (PersistentVolume), and the developer requests storage (PersistentVolumeClaim). Kubernetes automatically binds matching PVs to PVCs based on size, access mode, and StorageClass.

The PV/PVC Model — Admin vs Developer Responsibilities
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  THE PV / PVC MODEL — SEPARATION OF CONCERNS                            │
  │                                                                          │
  │  🔧 CLUSTER ADMIN                    👨‍💻 DEVELOPER                       │
  │  "I provision storage"               "I request storage"                 │
  │                                                                          │
  │  ┌──────────────────────┐           ┌──────────────────────┐            │
  │  │  PersistentVolume    │           │  PersistentVolume    │            │
  │  │  (PV)                │           │  Claim (PVC)         │            │
  │  │                      │           │                      │            │
  │  │  capacity: 10Gi      │           │  request: 5Gi        │            │
  │  │  accessModes:        │           │  accessModes:        │            │
  │  │    - ReadWriteOnce   │◀─── BIND ─▶│    - ReadWriteOnce   │            │
  │  │  storageClass: fast  │           │  storageClass: fast  │            │
  │  │  hostPath:           │           │                      │            │
  │  │    /data/postgres    │           │                      │            │
  │  └──────────────────────┘           └──────────┬───────────┘            │
  │                                                │                        │
  │  Admin doesn't need to know                    │ Developer doesn't      │
  │  WHICH pod will use it                         │ need to know WHERE     │
  │                                                │ the storage is         │
  │                                                ▼                        │
  │                                     ┌──────────────────────┐            │
  │                                     │  Pod / Deployment    │            │
  │                                     │                      │            │
  │                                     │  volumes:            │            │
  │                                     │  - persistentVolume  │            │
  │                                     │    Claim:            │            │
  │                                     │    claimName: my-pvc │            │
  │                                     │                      │            │
  │                                     │  volumeMounts:       │            │
  │                                     │  - mountPath: /data  │            │
  │                                     └──────────────────────┘            │
  │                                                                          │
  │  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════     │
  │  BINDING RULES:                                                          │
  │  ✅ PVC.request ≤ PV.capacity        (size must fit)                    │
  │  ✅ PVC.accessModes ⊆ PV.accessModes (modes must match)                │
  │  ✅ PVC.storageClass = PV.storageClass (class must match)               │
  │  ❌ No match? → PVC stays "Pending" until a matching PV appears        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1
Admin Creates PV

Defines capacity, access modes, reclaim policy, and points to actual storage (hostPath, NFS, cloud disk)

2
Developer Creates PVC

Requests storage size and access mode. Doesn't need to know where storage lives.

3
Kubernetes Binds

Finds a PV that matches the PVC's requirements. PVC status changes from Pending → Bound.

4
Pod Mounts PVC

Pod references the PVC by name. The bound PV's storage appears at the specified mountPath.

5
Data Persists ✅

Pod dies, restarts, gets rescheduled — PVC binding survives. New pod mounts same data.

🔬 PV/PVC Status Lifecycle

📋 Available
PV exists but no PVC has claimed it yet. It's ready to be bound.
🔗 Bound
PV is bound to a PVC. One-to-one relationship. The PV is now in use.
🔓 Released
PVC was deleted but PV still has data from the old claim. Admin must manually reclaim it (if Retain policy).
❌ Failed
Automatic reclamation failed. PV needs manual intervention.

22.2 Creating PersistentVolumes

A PersistentVolume is a cluster-level resource — it doesn't belong to any namespace. The admin creates it with a specific capacity, access mode, reclaim policy, and storage backend.

pv-hostpath.yaml 
# PersistentVolume with hostPath (for local testing / CKA exam)
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: easypj-data-pv           # ◀── cluster-scoped, no namespace
  labels:
    type: local
    app: easypj
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 10Gi                 # ◀── total storage this PV provides
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce                 # ◀── can be mounted read-write by ONE node
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain    # ◀── keep data when PVC deleted
  storageClassName: manual        # ◀── must match PVC's storageClassName
  hostPath:
    path: /data/easypj-postgres   # ◀── directory on the node
    type: DirectoryOrCreate
Access Mode Abbreviation Meaning Typical Use
ReadWriteOnce RWO Read-write by a single node Databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL)
ReadOnlyMany ROX Read-only by multiple nodes Shared config, static assets
ReadWriteMany RWX Read-write by multiple nodes Shared uploads, NFS-backed
ReadWriteOncePod RWOP Read-write by a single pod Exclusive access (K8s 1.29+)
⚠️ Access Modes Are About NODES, Not Pods

ReadWriteOnce means only one node can mount the volume for writing. Multiple pods on that same node CAN all mount it. This is a common CKA misconception. For true single-pod exclusivity, use ReadWriteOncePod (v1.29+).

Reclaim Policy What Happens When PVC Deleted Use When
Retain PV keeps data, status → Released. Admin must manually clean up and re-provision. Production databases, critical data you can't lose
Delete PV AND underlying storage deleted automatically. Data is gone. Dynamic provisioning, temporary/recreatable data
Recycle Runs rm -rf on the volume and makes it Available again. Deprecated. Don't use — deprecated since K8s 1.15
pv-nfs.yaml 
# PersistentVolume backed by NFS (multi-node shared storage)
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: easypj-uploads-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 20Gi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteMany                 # ◀── NFS supports multi-node read-write
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: nfs
  nfs:
    server: 192.168.1.100         # ◀── NFS server IP
    path: /exports/easypj-uploads # ◀── shared directory on NFS server

22.3 Creating PersistentVolumeClaims

A PVC is the developer's side of the equation — a request for storage. Unlike PVs (cluster-scoped), PVCs are namespaced. When you create a PVC, Kubernetes searches for a PV that meets the requirements. If found, the PVC binds to it. If not, the PVC stays in Pending state.

pvc-postgres.yaml 
# PVC requesting storage for easypj PostgreSQL database
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: easypj-postgres-pvc      # ◀── namespaced resource
  namespace: easypj-production
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce                 # ◀── must match PV's access modes
  storageClassName: manual        # ◀── must match PV's storageClassName
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi                # ◀── must be ≤ PV's capacity (10Gi)
# Binding: K8s finds easypj-data-pv (10Gi, RWO, manual) → MATCH → Bound!
PVC Binding Logic — How Kubernetes Matches PVCs to PVs
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  PVC BINDING DECISION TREE                                               │
  │                                                                          │
  │  New PVC created: requests 5Gi, RWO, storageClass: "manual"             │
  │       │                                                                  │
  │       ▼                                                                  │
  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐                           │
  │  │  Step 1: Filter by storageClassName       │                           │
  │  │  Looking for PVs with class = "manual"    │                           │
  │  └────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘                           │
  │                   │                                                      │
  │       ┌───────────┴───────────┐                                         │
  │       ▼                       ▼                                         │
  │  ┌─────────┐            ┌─────────┐                                    │
  │  │ PV-A    │            │ PV-B    │                                    │
  │  │ 10Gi    │            │ 5Gi     │                                    │
  │  │ manual  │ ✅          │ fast    │ ❌ wrong class                     │
  │  └────┬────┘            └─────────┘                                    │
  │       │                                                                  │
  │       ▼                                                                  │
  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐                           │
  │  │  Step 2: Filter by accessModes            │                           │
  │  │  PVC needs RWO → PV-A has RWO?           │                           │
  │  │  YES ✅                                   │                           │
  │  └────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘                           │
  │                   │                                                      │
  │       ▼                                                                  │
  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐                           │
  │  │  Step 3: Check capacity                   │                           │
  │  │  PVC requests 5Gi ≤ PV-A has 10Gi?       │                           │
  │  │  YES ✅                                   │                           │
  │  └────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘                           │
  │                   │                                                      │
  │       ▼                                                                  │
  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐                           │
  │  │  ✅ BOUND!                                │                           │
  │  │  PVC → PV-A                               │                           │
  │  │  PVC gets full 10Gi (even though it       │                           │
  │  │  only asked for 5Gi — smallest match)     │                           │
  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘                           │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
💡 CKA Debugging: PVC Stuck in Pending

If a PVC shows Pending status, run kubectl describe pvc <name> and check the Events section. Common causes:

  • No PV with matching storageClassName
  • No PV with sufficient capacity
  • No PV with matching access modes
  • All matching PVs are already Bound to other PVCs
  • If using dynamic provisioning: the StorageClass provisioner is not installed
Verify PV/PVC binding 
# Check PV and PVC status
kubectl get pv
# NAME              CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   RECLAIM POLICY   STATUS   CLAIM
# easypj-data-pv    10Gi       RWO            Retain           Bound    easypj-production/easypj-postgres-pvc

kubectl get pvc -n easypj-production
# NAME                   STATUS   VOLUME            CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES
# easypj-postgres-pvc    Bound    easypj-data-pv    10Gi       RWO

# Debug a Pending PVC
kubectl describe pvc easypj-postgres-pvc -n easypj-production
# Events:
#   Warning  ProvisioningFailed  no persistent volumes available for this claim

22.4 Using PVCs in Pods

Once a PVC is Bound, you reference it in your Pod spec exactly like any other volume. The pod doesn't know or care whether the PVC is backed by a local disk, NFS, or cloud storage — it just mounts a directory.

deployment-with-pvc.yaml 
# easypj Deployment using PVC for PostgreSQL data
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: easypj-web
  namespace: easypj-production
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: easypj
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: easypj
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: django
        image: easypj:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8000
        volumeMounts:
        - name: user-uploads          # ◀── mount name (matches volumes[])
          mountPath: /app/media       # ◀── path INSIDE the container
        - name: static-files
          mountPath: /app/staticfiles
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: user-uploads            # ◀── references the PVC
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: easypj-uploads-pvc   # ◀── name of the PVC
      - name: static-files
        configMap:
          name: easypj-static-config
Complete Flow: PV → PVC → Pod → Container Mount
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  COMPLETE MOUNT FLOW                                                     │
  │                                                                          │
  │  PersistentVolume          PVC                   Pod                     │
  │  ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────┐       │
  │  │ easypj-pv    │    │ easypj-pvc   │    │ easypj-web-abc       │       │
  │  │              │    │              │    │                      │       │
  │  │ /data/uploads│◀──▶│ BOUND        │◀───│ volumes:             │       │
  │  │ on node disk │    │              │    │ - pvc: easypj-pvc   │       │
  │  │              │    │              │    │                      │       │
  │  │ 10Gi, RWO    │    │ 5Gi request  │    │ containers:          │       │
  │  └──────────────┘    └──────────────┘    │ - volumeMounts:      │       │
  │                                          │   - /app/media ◀─┐  │       │
  │                                          └──────────────────┼──┘       │
  │                                                             │           │
  │  What the container sees:                                   │           │
  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                       │           │
  │  │  / (container root)              │                       │           │
  │  │  ├── app/                        │                       │           │
  │  │  │   ├── manage.py               │                       │           │
  │  │  │   ├── easypj/                 │                       │           │
  │  │  │   └── media/ ◀───────────────────── PVC mounted here  │           │
  │  │  │       ├── resumes/            │                       │           │
  │  │  │       │   └── john_doe.pdf    │   Data on external    │           │
  │  │  │       └── photos/             │   storage, not in     │           │
  │  │  │           └── profile.jpg     │   the container!      │           │
  │  │  └── ...                         │                       │           │
  │  └──────────────────────────────────┘                       │           │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
📖 PVC Must Be in the Same Namespace as the Pod

PVCs are namespaced resources. A pod in easypj-production can only mount PVCs that also exist in easypj-production. PVs themselves are cluster-scoped, but the PVC (the claim) must be co-located with the pod.

22.5 StorageClasses — Dynamic Provisioning

StorageClasses eliminate the need for an admin to pre-create PVs. When a developer creates a PVC with a storageClassName, and that class has a provisioner, Kubernetes automatically creates a matching PV on the fly. This is how most production clusters work.

Static vs Dynamic Provisioning
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  STATIC PROVISIONING (manual)        DYNAMIC PROVISIONING (automatic)    │
  │                                                                          │
  │  ┌─────────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────────┐            │
  │  │ 1. Admin creates PV │            │ 1. Admin creates     │            │
  │  │    (10Gi, RWO, host)│            │    StorageClass      │            │
  │  └─────────┬───────────┘            │    (provisioner,     │            │
  │            │                        │     params)          │            │
  │            ▼                        └──────────┬───────────┘            │
  │  ┌─────────────────────┐                       │  (one-time setup)      │
  │  │ 2. Dev creates PVC  │                       │                        │
  │  │    (5Gi, RWO)       │                       ▼                        │
  │  └─────────┬───────────┘            ┌──────────────────────┐            │
  │            │                        │ 2. Dev creates PVC   │            │
  │            ▼                        │    with storageClass │            │
  │  ┌─────────────────────┐            └──────────┬───────────┘            │
  │  │ 3. K8s binds        │                       │                        │
  │  │    PVC → PV         │                       ▼                        │
  │  └─────────┬───────────┘            ┌──────────────────────┐            │
  │            │                        │ 3. StorageClass auto │            │
  │            ▼                        │    creates PV! 🎉    │            │
  │  ┌─────────────────────┐            └──────────┬───────────┘            │
  │  │ 4. Pod mounts PVC   │                       │                        │
  │  └─────────────────────┘                       ▼                        │
  │                                     ┌──────────────────────┐            │
  │  Every new PVC = admin must         │ 4. Auto-bind + mount │            │
  │  manually create a PV first 😰     └──────────────────────┘            │
  │                                                                          │
  │                                     Admin sets up ONCE.                  │
  │                                     Every new PVC = auto PV! 🎉        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
storageclass.yaml 
# StorageClass for dynamic provisioning
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-ssd                      # ◀── the name PVCs reference
provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner  # ◀── for local testing
#provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com         # ◀── AWS EBS

#provisioner: pd.csi.storage.gke.io   # ◀── GCE Persistent Disk

#provisioner: disk.csi.azure.com      # ◀── Azure Disk

reclaimPolicy: Delete                  # ◀── auto-delete PV when PVC deleted
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer  # ◀── delay binding until pod scheduled
allowVolumeExpansion: true             # ◀── allow PVC resize
pvc-dynamic.yaml 
# PVC using dynamic provisioning — no PV needed, auto-created!
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: easypj-dynamic-pvc
  namespace: easypj-production
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: fast-ssd          # ◀── references StorageClass above
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 10Gi
# Result: StorageClass provisioner creates a 10Gi PV automatically
# PVC binds to the new PV → Ready to use in pods!
Feature Static Provisioning Dynamic Provisioning
PV creation Manual by admin Automatic by StorageClass
Admin workload High — create PV per request Low — one-time StorageClass setup
Storage waste PVs may sit unused PV created on-demand, no waste
CKA exam ✅ Tested (manual PV+PVC) ✅ Tested (StorageClass config)
Production use Rare (legacy/special cases) Standard practice in most clusters
💡 Default StorageClass

Most clusters have a default StorageClass. If you create a PVC without specifying storageClassName, the default class is used automatically. Check with kubectl get storageclass — the default has (default) annotation. On the CKA exam, there's usually a default class already configured.

22.6 PostgreSQL Storage for easypj

Let's put everything together: a complete production storage setup for PostgreSQL backing our easypj/jobpost Django application. This uses a StorageClass, PVC via volumeClaimTemplates in a StatefulSet, and proper data directory mounting.

Complete easypj PostgreSQL Storage Architecture
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  easypj POSTGRESQL STORAGE — COMPLETE SETUP                              │
  │                                                                          │
  │  StorageClass: "postgres-storage"                                        │
  │  ┌────────────────────────────────┐                                      │
  │  │  provisioner: local/hostPath   │                                      │
  │  │  reclaimPolicy: Retain         │ ◀── never delete DB data            │
  │  │  volumeBindingMode: WFFC       │                                      │
  │  └──────────────┬─────────────────┘                                      │
  │                 │ creates PV automatically                               │
  │                 ▼                                                         │
  │  PersistentVolumeClaim: "postgres-data-postgres-0"                       │
  │  ┌────────────────────────────────┐                                      │
  │  │  10Gi, ReadWriteOnce           │                                      │
  │  │  storageClass: postgres-storage│                                      │
  │  │  STATUS: Bound ✅              │                                      │
  │  └──────────────┬─────────────────┘                                      │
  │                 │ mounted into                                           │
  │                 ▼                                                         │
  │  StatefulSet: "postgres"                                                 │
  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐             │
  │  │  Pod: postgres-0                                       │             │
  │  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │             │
  │  │  │  Container: postgres                              │  │             │
  │  │  │  image: postgres:15                               │  │             │
  │  │  │                                                    │  │             │
  │  │  │  /var/lib/postgresql/data  ◀── PVC mounted here   │  │             │
  │  │  │  ├── base/        (databases)                     │  │             │
  │  │  │  ├── global/      (cluster-wide tables)           │  │             │
  │  │  │  ├── pg_wal/      (write-ahead logs)              │  │             │
  │  │  │  └── postgresql.conf                              │  │             │
  │  │  │                                                    │  │             │
  │  │  │  Data survives:                                    │  │             │
  │  │  │  ✅ Container restart                              │  │             │
  │  │  │  ✅ Pod deletion                                   │  │             │
  │  │  │  ✅ StatefulSet scaling                            │  │             │
  │  │  │  ✅ Rolling updates                                │  │             │
  │  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │             │
  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘             │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
easypj-postgres-complete.yaml 
# ── 1. StorageClass ──
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: postgres-storage
provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner
reclaimPolicy: Retain                 # ◀── NEVER auto-delete DB data
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
---
# ── 2. PersistentVolume (for local/exam clusters) ──
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: postgres-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 10Gi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: postgres-storage
  hostPath:
    path: /data/postgres
    type: DirectoryOrCreate
---
# ── 3. StatefulSet with volumeClaimTemplates ──
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: postgres
  namespace: easypj-production
spec:
  serviceName: postgres               # ◀── headless service name
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: postgres
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: postgres
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: postgres:15
        ports:
        - containerPort: 5432
        env:
        - name: POSTGRES_DB
          value: easypj_db
        - name: POSTGRES_USER
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: postgres-credentials
              key: username
        - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: postgres-credentials
              key: password
        - name: PGDATA                 # ◀── PostgreSQL data subdirectory
          value: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
        volumeMounts:
        - name: postgres-data          # ◀── matches volumeClaimTemplates
          mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 256Mi
          limits:
            cpu: "1"
            memory: 1Gi
  volumeClaimTemplates:                # ◀── auto-creates PVC per replica
  - metadata:
      name: postgres-data              # ◀── PVC name = postgres-data-postgres-0
    spec:
      accessModes:
      - ReadWriteOnce
      storageClassName: postgres-storage
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 10Gi
---
# ── 4. Headless Service for StatefulSet ──
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: postgres
  namespace: easypj-production
spec:
  clusterIP: None                      # ◀── headless = direct pod DNS
  selector:
    app: postgres
  ports:
  - port: 5432
# DNS: postgres-0.postgres.easypj-production.svc.cluster.local
Verify the complete setup 
# Apply the complete storage stack
kubectl apply -f easypj-postgres-complete.yaml

# Verify StorageClass
kubectl get storageclass postgres-storage
# NAME               PROVISIONER                    RECLAIMPOLICY
# postgres-storage   kubernetes.io/no-provisioner   Retain

# Verify PV is bound
kubectl get pv postgres-pv
# NAME          CAPACITY   ACCESS   STATUS   CLAIM
# postgres-pv   10Gi       RWO      Bound    easypj-production/postgres-data-postgres-0

# Verify PVC is bound
kubectl get pvc -n easypj-production
# NAME                       STATUS   VOLUME        CAPACITY
# postgres-data-postgres-0   Bound    postgres-pv   10Gi

# Verify pod is running with mounted volume
kubectl describe pod postgres-0 -n easypj-production | grep -A5 "Mounts:"
#     Mounts:
#       /var/lib/postgresql/data from postgres-data (rw)

# Test data persistence: kill the pod, check data survives
kubectl delete pod postgres-0 -n easypj-production
# StatefulSet recreates postgres-0 → PVC re-mounts → data intact! ✅
🏋️ CKA Practice Scenario: Create PV and PVC from Scratch

Task: Create a PersistentVolume named exam-pv with 2Gi capacity, ReadWriteOnce, storageClass manual, backed by hostPath /mnt/data. Then create a PVC named exam-pvc requesting 1Gi from that PV. Verify binding.

CKA Solution 
# Step 1: Create PV
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: exam-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 2Gi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/data
EOF

# Step 2: Create PVC
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: exam-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: manual
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
EOF

# Step 3: Verify binding
kubectl get pv exam-pv
# STATUS: Bound   CLAIM: default/exam-pvc ✅

kubectl get pvc exam-pvc
# STATUS: Bound   VOLUME: exam-pv ✅

🔄 PersistentVolume State Machine — Complete Lifecycle

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  PV LIFECYCLE STATE MACHINE                                              │
  │                                                                          │
  │                   ┌──────────────┐                                       │
  │                   │  PV Created  │                                       │
  │                   │  by Admin    │                                       │
  │                   └──────┬───────┘                                       │
  │                          │                                               │
  │                          ▼                                               │
  │               ┌──────────────────┐                                       │
  │         ┌────▶│   AVAILABLE ☁️    │ No PVC has claimed this PV           │
  │         │     └────────┬─────────┘                                       │
  │         │              │ PVC created with matching criteria               │
  │         │              ▼                                                  │
  │         │     ┌──────────────────┐                                       │
  │         │     │    BOUND 🔗      │ PV bound to PVC (1:1 relationship)    │
  │         │     └────────┬─────────┘                                       │
  │         │              │ PVC deleted                                      │
  │         │              ▼                                                  │
  │         │     ┌──────────────────┐                                       │
  │         │     │   RELEASED 🔓   │ PV still has old data                  │
  │         │     └────────┬─────────┘                                       │
  │         │              │                                                  │
  │         │    ┌─────────┴─────────┐                                       │
  │         │    │                   │                                        │
  │         │    ▼                   ▼                                        │
  │         │  Retain policy      Delete policy                              │
  │         │  ┌────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐                           │
  │         │  │Admin must  │     │PV + storage  │                           │
  │         │  │clean up PV │     │deleted auto  │                           │
  │         │  │manually    │     │💀 Data gone! │                           │
  │         │  └─────┬──────┘     └──────────────┘                           │
  │         │        │ kubectl delete pv + recreate                           │
  │         └────────┘                                                       │
  │                                                                          │
  │  ❌ FAILED: Auto-reclaim failed → admin must fix manually               │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
📊 Storage Capacity Planning — easypj
  • PostgreSQL data: 10Gi (grows ~1Gi/month with 10K job posts)
  • User uploads (resumes): 20Gi (avg 200KB × 100K files)
  • Static files (CSS/JS): emptyDir (regenerated, ~50MB)
  • Redis cache: emptyDir with medium: Memory (256Mi)
  • Logs: emptyDir (100Mi, forwarded to log aggregator)
  • Total persistent storage needed: ~30Gi
⌨️ Chapter 22 — Must-Know kubectl Commands
  • kubectl get pv — list all PVs (cluster-wide)
  • kubectl get pvc -A — list PVCs across all namespaces
  • kubectl describe pvc <name> — debug binding issues
  • kubectl get sc — list StorageClasses
  • kubectl patch pv <name> -p '{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy":"Retain"}}' — change reclaim policy
  • kubectl get events --field-selector reason=ProvisioningFailed — find provisioning errors
💡 CKA Time-Saver: PVC Expansion

If a PVC needs more storage and the StorageClass has allowVolumeExpansion: true, you can simply kubectl edit pvc <name> and increase requests.storage. The PV resizes automatically (for cloud-backed storage). On the CKA exam, check if expansion is enabled: kubectl get sc <name> -o yaml | grep allowVolumeExpansion.

Under the Hood — How PVs and PVCs Bind: The Matching Algorithm, Access Modes, Dynamic Provisioning, and CSI Driver Architecture
🗺️ PV-PVC Binding Algorithm — How Kubernetes Matches Claims to Volumes

The persistent volume controller runs a matching loop that pairs PVCs with PVs. Understanding the exact matching criteria helps you debug "PVC stuck in Pending" issues.

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PV-PVC BINDING ALGORITHM — Step by Step                                     │
│                                                                              │
│  PVC: easypj-media (requests: storage=10Gi, accessModes=[RWO])               │
│  Available PVs:                                                               │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ PV-1: 100Gi, RWO, Retain    PV-2: 10Gi, RWO, Delete                │    │
│  │ PV-3: 10Gi, RWX, Retain     PV-4: 5Gi,  RWO, Retain                │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                              │
│  STEP 1: FILTER by storage size (PVC requests 10Gi)                          │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ PV-1: 100Gi >= 10Gi ✅     PV-2: 10Gi >= 10Gi ✅                    │    │
│  │ PV-3: 10Gi >= 10Gi ✅     PV-4: 5Gi >= 10Gi  ❌ (too small)        │    │
│  │ Remaining: PV-1, PV-2, PV-3                                          │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                              │
│  STEP 2: FILTER by access mode (PVC requests RWO)                             │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ PV-1: RWO ✅              PV-2: RWO ✅                               │    │
│  │ PV-3: RWX ✅ (RWX includes RWO capability)                           │    │
│  │ Remaining: PV-1, PV-2, PV-3                                          │    │
│  │                                                                      │    │
│  │ ACCESS MODE COMPATIBILITY:                                            │    │
│  │ ┌──────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │    │
│  │ │ RWO      │ ReadWriteOnce — single node read/write             │    │    │
│  │ │ ROX      │ ReadOnlyMany — many nodes read only               │    │    │
│  │ │ RWX      │ ReadWriteMany — many nodes read/write              │    │    │
│  │ │ RWOP     │ ReadWriteOncePod — single pod (new in 1.29)        │    │    │
│  │ └──────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                              │
│  STEP 3: SELECT best match (smallest sufficient PV wins)                     │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ PV-1: 100Gi → EXCESSIVE (wastes 90Gi)                               │    │
│  │ PV-2: 10Gi  → PERFECT MATCH 🏆 (exact size)                        │    │
│  │ PV-3: 10Gi  → Also matches, but PV-2 selected first                 │    │
│  │                                                                      │    │
│  │ SELECTION RULES:                                                     │    │
│  │ 1. Smallest PV >= PVC request wins                                   │    │
│  │ 2. If same size, PV created earliest wins                            │    │
│  │ 3. Binding is EXCLUSIVE — one PV = one PVC                           │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                              │
│  AFTER BINDING:                                                              │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ PVC status: Bound → PV-2                                              │    │
│  │ PV status:   Bound → Claim: default/easypj-media                     │    │
│  │ PV-2 is now UNAVAILABLE for any other PVC                             │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                              │
│  ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════     │
│  STORAGECLASS — Dynamic Provisioning:                                        │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ Without StorageClass: Admin creates PV manually → PVC binds          │    │
│  │ With StorageClass:     PVC specifies StorageClass → provisioner      │    │
│  │                        AUTO-CREATES PV → PVC binds automatically     │    │
│  │                                                                      │    │
│  │  CSI (Container Storage Interface) Drivers:                          │    │
│  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │    │
│  │  │ 1. PVC created with storageClassName: aws-ebs               │     │    │
│  │  │ 2. StorageClass provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com                │     │    │
│  │  │ 3. CSI provisioner calls AWS API: CreateVolume(10Gi)        │     │    │
│  │  │ 4. AWS creates EBS volume → returns volumeID                 │     │    │
│  │  │ 5. CSI creates PV object with volumeHandle=<volumeID>       │     │    │
│  │  │ 6. PV binds to PVC                                             │     │    │
│  │  │ 7. Pod created → CSI node plugin ATTACHES volume to node    │     │    │
│  │  │ 8. CSI node plugin MOUNTS volume into container              │     │    │
│  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                              │
│  ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════     │
│  RECLAIM POLICIES — What Happens When PVC Is Deleted:                        │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ Retain:  PV stays (Released). Admin must MANUALLY delete + clean    │    │
│  │          up underlying storage. Data persists.                       │    │
│  │ Delete:  PV + underlying storage DELETED automatically. Data gone.  │    │
│  │ Recycle: DEPRECATED. Was: scrub data (rm -rf) → make Available.    │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
🔑 CKA Insight: PVC stuck in Pending? Check: (1) kubectl describe pvc — what's the error? "no persistent volumes available" = create a PV or StorageClass. (2) kubectl get pv — any Available PVs with sufficient capacity and matching access mode? (3) StorageClass with volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer delays binding until a pod uses the PVC — this is NORMAL (pod must be scheduled first for topology-aware provisioning).

🔑 Key Takeaways

Bulleted key takeaways go here.

⚠️ Common Gotchas & Misconceptions
  • ❌ PVC size must exactly match PV size
  • ✅ PVC request must be ≤ PV capacity — K8s picks the smallest matching PV
  • ❌ ReadWriteOnce means only one pod can mount it
  • ✅ RWO means one NODE. Multiple pods on same node can all mount it
  • storageClassName must match EXACTLY between PV and PVC — empty string ≠ omitted
  • PV is cluster-scoped but PVC is namespaced — pod and PVC must be in same namespace
  • Recycle reclaim policy is deprecated — use Retain or Delete
  • After PVC deletion with Retain policy, PV stays Released — must delete and recreate PV to reuse
  • PVC stuck in Pending — Top 3 causes: (1) No PV matches the requested size/accessMode, (2) StorageClass name mismatch, (3) No default StorageClass and PVC doesn't specify one. Debug with kubectl describe pvc
  • Access modes must match — PV offers ReadWriteOnce but PVC requests ReadWriteMany? Won't bind. Know the modes: RWO (single node), ROX (many nodes read-only), RWX (many nodes read-write)
  • Reclaim policies — Retain: PV data preserved after PVC deletion (manual cleanup). Delete: PV and backing storage removed. Recycle: deprecated. Default for dynamic PVs is Delete — dangerous for production!
  • storageClassName: "" vs omitting it — Empty string means "no StorageClass" (only matches PVs with no class). Omitting it uses the cluster's default StorageClass. This subtle difference is a classic CKA trap
  • PV is cluster-scoped, PVC is namespace-scoped — kubectl get pv (no -n flag needed). kubectl get pvc -n <ns>. A PVC in namespace prod can bind to any available PV
⚡ Speed Tips

CKA Speed Tip — PV/PVC binding checklist (memorize this):
For a PVC to bind to a PV, ALL must match:
✅ Sufficient capacity (PV size ≥ PVC request)
✅ Compatible access mode (at least one in common)
✅ Matching StorageClass (or both empty)
✅ PV status must be Available (not Released or Bound)
✅ Label selectors match (if PVC uses selector)

🔑 Commands to Know (Chapter 22)

ActionCommand
List PVs (cluster-wide)kubectl get pv
List PVCs in namespacekubectl get pvc -n <namespace>
List PVCs all namespaceskubectl get pvc -A
Debug Pending PVCkubectl describe pvc <name> -n <ns>
List StorageClasseskubectl get storageclass (or kubectl get sc)
Check PV detailskubectl describe pv <name>
Change reclaim policykubectl patch pv <name> -p '{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy":"Retain"}}'
Delete PVkubectl delete pv <name>
PVs sorted by sizekubectl get pv --sort-by=.spec.capacity.storage
annotation)kubectl get sc / (default)
unstick a terminating PVC (last resort)kubectl delete pvc <name> --grace-period=0 --force
🧪 Drill

Timed challenge (target: 8 minutes):

  • 1. Create a PV: 5Gi, ReadWriteOnce, hostPath: /mnt/data, reclaim policy Retain
  • 2. Create a PVC requesting 3Gi with ReadWriteOnce — verify it binds
  • 3. Create a pod that mounts the PVC at /data
  • 4. Write a file, delete the pod, recreate it — verify data persists
  • 5. Delete the PVC — check PV status (should be Released, not Available)
  • 6. Create a StorageClass with provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner and volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer

🧠 Chapter 22 — Lab Q&A · Concept Check

Concept-check questions go here.

⚙️ Chapter 22 — Scenario & Command Drills (11)

Quick recall of the PV/PVC binding lifecycle — each with a full answer & explanation.

Q1
Create a PersistentVolume with 10Gi capacity, ReadWriteOnce access mode, hostPath at /mnt/data, and reclaim policy Retain.
Show Answer
Answer
yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
name: pv-data
# Note: PVs are cluster-scoped — no namespace!
spec:
capacity:
storage: 10Gi
accessModes:
- ReadWriteOnce            # ← Single node read-write
persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain   # ← Keep data after PVC deletion
hostPath:
path: /mnt/data
type: DirectoryOrCreate

# Apply and verify:
kubectl apply -f pv.yaml
kubectl get pv pv-data
# NAME     CAPACITY  ACCESS MODES  RECLAIM POLICY  STATUS     AGE
# pv-data  10Gi      RWO           Retain          Available  5s

# Access mode abbreviations:
# RWO = ReadWriteOnce (single node)
# ROX = ReadOnlyMany  (many nodes, read-only)
# RWX = ReadWriteMany (many nodes, read-write)
# RWOP = ReadWriteOncePod (single pod, K8s 1.22+)
Explanation

PersistentVolumes are cluster-scoped resources (no namespace). Key fields: capacity (must match/exceed PVC request), accessModes (must be compatible), persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy (what happens when PVC is deleted). Retain preserves data for manual cleanup, Delete removes backing storage. On the CKA, hostPath is the most common PV type (lab environments). Always use Retain for important data — the default for dynamically provisioned PVs is Delete!

Q2
Create a PVC that binds to the PV from Q1. Then create a pod that mounts it at /data.
Show Answer
Answer
pvc
# PVC:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
name: pvc-data
namespace: default         # ← PVCs are namespace-scoped!
spec:
accessModes:
- ReadWriteOnce            # ← Must match PV
resources:
requests:
  storage: 5Gi           # ← Can be ≤ PV capacity (10Gi)
# storageClassName: ""     # ← Omit for static binding

---
# Pod using the PVC:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
name: data-pod
spec:
volumes:
- name: data-vol
persistentVolumeClaim:
  claimName: pvc-data    # ← Reference the PVC name
containers:
- name: app
image: nginx
volumeMounts:
- name: data-vol
  mountPath: /data

# Verify binding:
kubectl get pvc pvc-data
# NAME       STATUS  VOLUME   CAPACITY  ACCESS  AGE
# pvc-data   Bound   pv-data  10Gi      RWO     5s

kubectl get pv pv-data
# STATUS: Bound  ← PV is now bound to pvc-data
Explanation

PVC binding rules: PVC request ≤ PV capacity, access modes compatible, StorageClass matches. Once bound, the PVC gets the FULL PV capacity (5Gi requested but 10Gi available). The pod references the PVC by name in persistentVolumeClaim.claimName. On the CKA, the three-object chain is: PV (admin creates) → PVC (developer creates) → Pod (developer mounts PVC). If the PVC stays Pending, check: size, access mode, and StorageClass matching.

Q3
A PVC is stuck in Pending state. How do you diagnose the issue?
Show Answer
Answer
describe the pvc for events
# Step 1: Describe the PVC for events
kubectl describe pvc stuck-pvc
# Events:
#   "no persistent volumes available for this claim"
#   OR "storageclass 'fast' not found"

# Step 2: Check available PVs
kubectl get pv
# NAME     CAPACITY  ACCESS  RECLAIM  STATUS      CLASS    AGE
# pv-1     5Gi       RWO     Retain   Available   slow     5m
# pv-2     10Gi      ROX     Delete   Available   fast     5m
# pv-3     5Gi       RWO     Retain   Bound       -        5m  ← Already taken!

# Common causes:
# 1. No PV with enough capacity
kubectl get pvc stuck-pvc -o yaml | grep storage
#   requests: storage: 20Gi  ← But no PV ≥ 20Gi!

# 2. Access mode mismatch
# PVC requests RWX but PV only offers RWO

# 3. StorageClass mismatch
kubectl get pvc stuck-pvc -o yaml | grep storageClassName
# storageClassName: "premium"  ← No PV with class "premium"!

# 4. No default StorageClass
kubectl get sc
# No default → PVC with no class specified stays Pending

# 5. WaitForFirstConsumer binding mode
# PVC stays Pending until a pod references it — this is NORMAL!
kubectl get sc local-storage -o yaml | grep volumeBindingMode
# volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
Explanation

PVC Pending is the most common PV troubleshooting scenario on the CKA. Systematic approach: (1) describe the PVC for error events, (2) check available PVs for capacity/access/class, (3) verify StorageClass exists. Note that WaitForFirstConsumer is NOT a bug — the PVC intentionally stays Pending until a pod is created, so the PV can be provisioned on the same node as the pod. Always start with kubectl describe pvc.

Q4
What happens to a PV when its PVC is deleted? Explain all reclaim policies.
Show Answer
Answer
Policy PV Status After PVC Delete Data Next Steps
Retain Released Preserved Manual cleanup, edit PV to remove claimRef
Delete PV deleted Deleted Nothing — PV and data are gone
Recycle Available Scrubbed (rm -rf) Deprecated — don't use
to reuse a retained pv after pvc deletion
# To reuse a Retained PV after PVC deletion:
# 1. PV shows "Released" — can't bind a new PVC yet
kubectl get pv pv-data
# STATUS: Released

# 2. Remove the old claimRef:
kubectl patch pv pv-data -p '{"spec":{"claimRef":null}}'
# OR:
kubectl edit pv pv-data
# Delete the entire claimRef section

# 3. PV returns to Available:
kubectl get pv pv-data
# STATUS: Available ← Ready for new PVC

# Change reclaim policy on existing PV:
kubectl patch pv pv-data -p \
'{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy":"Retain"}}'
Explanation

Reclaim policy controls PV fate after PVC deletion. Retain is safest — data preserved, PV goes to Released state (NOT Available). To reuse a Released PV, you must remove the claimRef. Delete removes both PV and backing storage (default for dynamic provisioning — dangerous!). On the CKA, changing policy from Delete to Retain with kubectl patch is a common task. Know the Released → Available transition requires manual intervention.

Q5
Create a StorageClass with volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer. Why is this important?
Show Answer
Answer
yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
name: local-storage
provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner  # ← Manual provisioning
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer    # ← KEY!
reclaimPolicy: Retain

# What it does:
# Immediate (default):
#   PVC → PV binding happens immediately
#   PV might be on node-1
#   Pod gets scheduled to node-2
#   → Pod stuck Pending! PV is on wrong node!

# WaitForFirstConsumer:
#   PVC → Stays Pending (normal!)
#   Pod created → scheduler picks node-2
#   PV binding happens on node-2
#   → Pod starts successfully!

# Verify:
kubectl get sc local-storage
# NAME            PROVISIONER                    RECLAIMPOLICY  VOLUMEBINDINGMODE
# local-storage   kubernetes.io/no-provisioner   Retain         WaitForFirstConsumer

# PVC with this StorageClass:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
name: local-pvc
spec:
storageClassName: local-storage
accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
resources:
requests:
  storage: 5Gi
# This PVC stays Pending until a pod uses it!
Explanation

WaitForFirstConsumer delays PV binding until a pod using the PVC is scheduled. This is critical for local storage (hostPath, local PVs) to ensure the PV is on the same node as the pod. Without it, the PV could bind to a node where no pod runs. On the CKA, if you see a PVC stuck in Pending with WaitForFirstConsumer and NO pod using it — that's expected behavior, not an error. Create the pod and it will bind. kubernetes.io/no-provisioner means admins must manually create PVs.

Q6
What is the difference between storageClassName: "" and omitting storageClassName in a PVC?
Show Answer
Answer
scenario: cluster has a default storageclass…
# Scenario: Cluster has a default StorageClass "standard"

# Option 1: Omit storageClassName
spec:
accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
resources:
requests:
  storage: 5Gi
# storageClassName: ← not specified
# Result: Uses DEFAULT StorageClass ("standard")
# → Dynamic provisioning creates PV automatically

# Option 2: storageClassName: ""
spec:
accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
resources:
requests:
  storage: 5Gi
storageClassName: ""     # ← Explicitly empty
# Result: NO StorageClass used
# → Only binds to PVs that also have NO class
# → No dynamic provisioning

# Option 3: storageClassName: "fast"
spec:
storageClassName: "fast"
# Result: Only binds to PVs with class "fast"
# → Or dynamic provisioning via "fast" StorageClass

# Check default StorageClass:
kubectl get sc
# NAME                  PROVISIONER          AGE
# standard (default)    rancher.io/local     5d
#          ↑ "(default)" annotation
Explanation

This is one of the most subtle CKA traps. Omitting storageClassName uses the cluster's default StorageClass (dynamic provisioning). Setting storageClassName: "" explicitly means "no class" — only matches PVs with no class. On the CKA, if you want static binding to a specific PV without dynamic provisioning, use storageClassName: "". To check the default: kubectl get sc — look for (default) annotation.

Q7
Expand a PVC from 5Gi to 10Gi. What conditions must be met?
Show Answer
Answer
requirements for pvc expansion
# Requirements for PVC expansion:
# 1. StorageClass must have allowVolumeExpansion: true
kubectl get sc standard -o yaml | grep allowVolumeExpansion
# allowVolumeExpansion: true  ← Required!

# 2. Simply edit the PVC size:
kubectl edit pvc my-pvc
# Change: storage: 5Gi → storage: 10Gi

# Or use patch:
kubectl patch pvc my-pvc -p \
'{"spec":{"resources":{"requests":{"storage":"10Gi"}}}}'

# 3. Check status:
kubectl get pvc my-pvc
# CAPACITY: 10Gi ← Expanded!

# For some volume types, expansion requires pod restart:
kubectl describe pvc my-pvc
# Conditions:
#   Type: FileSystemResizePending
#   Message: Waiting for user to restart the pod

# Restart the pod:
kubectl delete pod my-pod
# Deployment recreates pod → filesystem expands

# ⚠️ Cannot SHRINK a PVC! Only expansion is supported.
Explanation

PVC expansion requires allowVolumeExpansion: true on the StorageClass. Just edit the PVC spec to request more storage. Some provisioners expand online (no pod restart needed), others need pod restart (check for FileSystemResizePending condition). On the CKA, this is a straightforward task but watch for: (1) StorageClass doesn't allow expansion (verify first), (2) can never shrink — only grow, (3) may need to restart the pod for filesystem-level resize.

Q8
How do you sort PersistentVolumes by capacity and find all PVCs across all namespaces?
Show Answer
Answer
sort pvs by capacity
# Sort PVs by capacity:
kubectl get pv --sort-by=.spec.capacity.storage
# NAME     CAPACITY  ACCESS  RECLAIM  STATUS     CLASS     AGE
# pv-sm    1Gi       RWO     Retain   Available  local     5m
# pv-md    5Gi       RWO     Delete   Bound      standard  10m
# pv-lg    20Gi      RWX     Retain   Available  fast      2m

# All PVCs in all namespaces:
kubectl get pvc -A
# NAMESPACE  NAME       STATUS  VOLUME  CAPACITY  ACCESS  AGE
# default    data-pvc   Bound   pv-md   5Gi       RWO     10m
# prod       db-pvc     Bound   pv-lg   20Gi      RWX     5m
# dev        cache-pvc  Pending -       -         -       2m

# Custom columns for overview:
kubectl get pv -o custom-columns=\
NAME:.metadata.name,\
SIZE:.spec.capacity.storage,\
STATUS:.status.phase,\
CLAIM:.spec.claimRef.name,\
CLASS:.spec.storageClassName

# Find which PV is bound to which PVC:
kubectl get pv -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.spec.claimRef.namespace}/{.spec.claimRef.name}{"\n"}{end}'
Explanation

PVs are cluster-scoped (no -n flag needed), PVCs are namespaced (-A to see all). --sort-by uses JSONPath for sorting. On the CKA, you may be asked to find a specific PV/PVC relationship — use the claimRef field on a PV to see which PVC it's bound to. Custom columns are faster than -o wide for specific information. Remember: kubectl get pv (no namespace), kubectl get pvc -n <ns> (needs namespace).

Q9
What is the difference between ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, and ReadWriteOncePod?
Show Answer
Answer
Mode Short Description Use Case
ReadWriteOnce RWO Read-write by ONE node Single database pod
ReadOnlyMany ROX Read-only by many nodes Shared config/static assets
ReadWriteMany RWX Read-write by many nodes Shared uploads (NFS,EFS)
ReadWriteOncePod RWOP Read-write by ONE pod Exclusive pod access (1.22+)
cka gotcha
# CKA gotcha:
# RWO = "one NODE" not "one pod"!
# Multiple pods on the SAME node can share an RWO volume
# RWOP = "one POD" — exclusive access guarantee

# hostPath supports: RWO only
# NFS supports: RWO, ROX, RWX
# AWS EBS supports: RWO only
# AWS EFS supports: RWX
Explanation

The biggest trap: ReadWriteOnce means one NODE, not one pod. Multiple pods on the same node CAN mount the same RWO volume simultaneously. For true single-pod exclusivity, use ReadWriteOncePod (K8s 1.22+). On the CKA, access mode mismatches are a top reason for PVC binding failure. If a PVC requests RWX but only RWO PVs exist, it stays Pending. Not all storage backends support all modes — hostPath only supports RWO.

Q10
A PV shows status Released after its PVC was deleted. How do you make it Available again for a new PVC?
Show Answer
Answer
check current state
# Check current state:
kubectl get pv pv-data
# NAME     CAPACITY  ACCESS  RECLAIM  STATUS    CLAIM               AGE
# pv-data  10Gi      RWO     Retain   Released  default/old-pvc     1h

# The PV has a claimRef to the old PVC — must remove it:
kubectl edit pv pv-data
# Delete the entire claimRef section:
# spec:
#   claimRef:          ← DELETE these 4 lines
#     apiVersion: v1
#     kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
#     name: old-pvc
#     namespace: default
#     uid: abc-123

# Or use patch:
kubectl patch pv pv-data --type json \
-p '[{"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/claimRef"}]'

# Verify:
kubectl get pv pv-data
# STATUS: Available ← Ready for new PVC!

# ⚠️ The data from the old PVC is still on disk!
# You may want to clean it before reuse:
# SSH to node → rm -rf /mnt/data/*
Explanation

When a PVC is deleted and the PV has Retain policy, the PV goes to Released (not Available). The claimRef still references the old PVC, preventing new bindings. Remove it to return to Available. On the CKA, this is a multi-step task: (1) identify the Released PV, (2) remove claimRef, (3) verify Available status. Note that old data remains — the admin must decide whether to clean it. This is why Retain requires manual intervention by design.

Q11
Write a StatefulSet with volumeClaimTemplates for a PostgreSQL database. How do volumeClaimTemplates differ from regular PVCs? What happens to the volumes when pods are deleted?
Show Answer
Answer
yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
name: postgres
spec:
serviceName: postgres-headless
replicas: 3
selector:
matchLabels:
  app: postgres
template:
metadata:
  labels:
    app: postgres
spec:
  containers:
  - name: postgres
    image: postgres:15
    ports:
    - containerPort: 5432
    volumeMounts:
    - name: pgdata
      mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
volumeClaimTemplates:         # ← Not under template!
- metadata:
  name: pgdata               # Matches volumeMount name
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  storageClassName: standard
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 10Gi

# What gets created:
# postgres-0 → PVC: pgdata-postgres-0 → PV (auto-provisioned)
# postgres-1 → PVC: pgdata-postgres-1 → PV (auto-provisioned)
# postgres-2 → PVC: pgdata-postgres-2 → PV (auto-provisioned)

# Key differences from regular PVCs:
# 1. Each pod gets its OWN unique PVC (not shared)
# 2. PVC name = <template-name>-<statefulset-name>-<ordinal>
# 3. PVCs are NOT deleted when pods or StatefulSet are deleted
# 4. When pod restarts, it reattaches to the SAME PVC

# Verify:
kubectl get pvc
# pgdata-postgres-0   Bound   pv-abc   10Gi   RWO    standard
# pgdata-postgres-1   Bound   pv-def   10Gi   RWO    standard
# pgdata-postgres-2   Bound   pv-ghi   10Gi   RWO    standard

# ⚠️ Deleting StatefulSet does NOT delete PVCs:
kubectl delete sts postgres
kubectl get pvc
# All PVCs still exist! Data is preserved.
# Manual cleanup: kubectl delete pvc pgdata-postgres-{0,1,2}
Explanation

volumeClaimTemplates are unique to StatefulSets and create a dedicated PVC per pod replica. Unlike Deployments where all pods share the same PVC (or have no persistent storage), StatefulSets guarantee that pod postgres-0 always gets pgdata-postgres-0. PVCs survive pod restarts, rescheduling, and even StatefulSet deletion — this is by design to prevent accidental data loss. On the CKA, remember: volumeClaimTemplates is a top-level field of StatefulSet spec (same level as template), NOT nested inside the pod template. The naming convention <vct-name>-<sts-name>-<ordinal> is deterministic.
