    -p '{"imagePullSecrets": [{"name": "ghcr-secret"}]}'
# Now EVERY pod using this ServiceAccount auto-gets ghcr-secret

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# VERIFY: Check if kubelet can pull using the secret
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
$ kubectl describe pod easypj-web-xxx -n easypj | grep -A5 "Pulling"
# Normal  Pulling   Pulling image "ghcr.io/youruser/easypj:v2.1"
# Normal  Pulled    Successfully pulled image  ← Secret works!
💡 CKA Exam Tip: imagePullSecrets

The CKA exam frequently tests imagePullSecrets. Remember: if you create a secret in namespace X and the pod is in namespace Y, the pod CANNOT use the secret. Secrets are namespace-scoped. Also, patching a ServiceAccount with imagePullSecrets only affects NEW pods — existing pods must be restarted.

37.2 GitOps with ArgoCD

CONCEPT

GitOps means Git is the single source of truth for your cluster state. Instead of running kubectl apply from a CI pipeline (push-based), a GitOps tool like ArgoCD watches your Git repo and syncs changes automatically (pull-based).

Traditional CI/CD (Push) vs GitOps (Pull)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  TRADITIONAL CI/CD (Push-Based):       GITOPS (Pull-Based):                 │
│                                                                              │
│  Developer pushes code                 Developer pushes code                 │
│       │                                     │                                │
│       ▼                                     ▼                                │
│  CI builds & tests                    CI builds & tests                    │
│       │                                     │                                │
│       ▼                                     ▼                                │
│  CD runs kubectl apply ⚠️              CD updates manifest                   │
│  (push to cluster directly)            in Git repo                           │
│       │                                     │                                │
│       ▼                                     ▼                                │
│  Deployed. But...                      ArgoCD detects Git change             │
│  - Who ran it? 🤷                            │                                │
│  - What changed? 🤷                          ▼                                │
│  - How to rollback? 😬                 ArgoCD syncs to cluster ✅            │
│  - Drift undetected 😱                                                       │
│                                         Benefits:                            │
│                                         ✅ Full audit trail (Git log)       │
│                                         ✅ Rollback = git revert             │
│                                         ✅ Drift detection & auto-fix      │
│                                         ✅ PR-based deployments              │
│                                         ✅ No cluster creds in CI           │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

ArgoCD Architecture

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ARGOCD SYNC LOOP                                                            │
│                                                                              │
│  ┌──────────────┐      Poll every 3min     ┌──────────────────┐            │
│  │              │   ◀─────────────────────  │                  │            │
│  │  Git Repo    │                           │    ArgoCD        │            │
│  │  (manifests) │   Detect diff?            │    Controller    │            │
│  │              │   ─────────────────────▶  │                  │            │
│  └──────────────┘                           └────────┬─────────┘            │
│                                                       │                      │
│         Git state ≠ Cluster state?                   │ Sync!                │
│         → OutOfSync status                           │                      │
│         → Auto-sync or manual approval               ▼                      │
│                                              ┌──────────────────┐           │
│                                              │   K8s Cluster    │           │
│                                              │   ┌──────────┐   │           │
│                                              │   │ easypj   │   │           │
│                                              │   │ pods     │   │           │
│                                              │   └──────────┘   │           │
│                                              │   Status: Synced │           │
│                                              │   Health: Healthy │           │
│                                              └──────────────────┘           │
│                                                                              │
│  ArgoCD UI Dashboard:                                                        │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐             │
│  │ App: easypj     │ Sync: ✅ Synced │ Health: 💚 Healthy    │             │
│  │ Repo: github.com/user/easypj-k8s   │ Revision: abc1234   │             │
│  │ Target: easypj namespace            │ Auto-Sync: ON       │             │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘             │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Webhooks vs Polling — Instant Sync

ArgoCD polls Git every 3 minutes by default. For instant deployment, configure a webhook in your Git provider (GitHub, GitLab, BitBucket) so ArgoCD syncs within seconds of a push:

Terminal — Webhook setup for ArgoCD 
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# GITHUB WEBHOOK CONFIGURATION
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# 1. Expose argocd-server (production uses Ingress/LB, not port-forward)
$ kubectl port-forward svc/argocd-server -n argocd 8080:443 &

# 2. Get ArgoCD admin password
$ ARGO_PASS=$(kubectl -n argocd get secret argocd-initial-admin-secret \
    -o jsonpath="{.data.password}" | base64 -d)

# 3. Login via CLI
$ argocd login localhost:8080 --username admin --password $ARGO_PASS --insecure

# 4. Set webhook on GitHub repo:
#    GitHub Repo → Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook
#    Payload URL: https://argocd.example.com/api/webhook
#    Content type: application/json
#    Events: Just the push event
#    Secret: <generate-a-random-string>

# 5. Configure webhook secret in ArgoCD
$ argocd admin settings rbac \
    --set argocd-secret.github-webhook-secret=<random-string>

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# TEST: Push to Git → ArgoCD syncs in <5 seconds!
# ═══════════════════════════════════════

ArgoCD RBAC — Who Can Sync What?

ArgoCD has its own RBAC layer — separate from Kubernetes RBAC. It controls who can access the ArgoCD UI/CLI and what actions they can perform on specific apps:

argocd-rbac-cm.yaml — ArgoCD RBAC Configuration 
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: argocd-rbac-cm
  namespace: argocd
data:
  # Default policy — deny all unless explicitly allowed
  policy.default: role:none

  # Scopes define permission granularity
  scopes: '[groups, email]'

  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # RBAC MATRIX — who can do what to which apps
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  policy.csv: |
    # Syntax: p, <subject>, <resource>, <action>, <object>
    # ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # TEAM BACKEND — full control over easypj
    p, role:backend-team, applications, *, easypj/*, allow
    p, role:backend-team, logs, get, easypj/*, allow

    # TEAM PLATFORM — read-only for all apps (monitoring)
    p, role:platform-team, applications, get, *, allow

    # CI BOT — sync-only (no manual access)
    p, role:ci-bot, applications, sync, easypj/*, allow

    # ADMIN — full control (use sparingly)
    g, admin@company.com, role:admin

    # ═══════════════════════════════════
    # SUBJECT RESOLUTION — SSO groups → roles
    # ═══════════════════════════════════
    g, backend@yourorg.com, role:backend-team
    g, platform@yourorg.com, role:platform-team

Sync Strategies — Automated, Manual, and Hybrid

ArgoCD Sync Strategy Comparison

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  SYNC STRATEGIES                                                             │
│                                                                              │
│  STRATEGY A: FULL AUTO-SYNC (dev / staging)                                  │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
│  │ syncPolicy:                                                     │        │
│  │   automated:                                                    │        │
│  │     prune: true        # Remove resources deleted from Git      │        │
│  │     selfHeal: true     # Auto-fix manual kubectl changes       │        │
│  │                                                                 │        │
│  │ Git push ──▶ Auto-sync ──▶ Cluster updated  (seconds)          │        │
│  │ Drift detected ──▶ Auto-heal ──▶ Back to Git state (seconds)   │        │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
│                                                                              │
│  STRATEGY B: MANUAL SYNC (production)                                        │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
│  │ syncPolicy: {}   # Empty — no automated sync                    │        │
│  │                                                                 │        │
│  │ Git push ──▶ ArgoCD shows OutOfSync ──▶ Human clicks Sync      │        │
│  │ Why? Release windows, change control, pre-sync approvals        │        │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
│                                                                              │
│  STRATEGY C: HYBRID (recommended for production)                             │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
│  │ syncPolicy:                                                     │        │
│  │   automated:                                                    │        │
│  │     prune: false       # NEVER auto-delete in prod              │        │
│  │     selfHeal: true     # Fix drift (someone ran kubectl)        │        │
│  │                                                                 │        │
│  │ Result: Drift auto-fixed. Resource deletions require manual     │        │
│  │         approval (PR + Sync button). Safe for production!       │        │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
│                                                                              │
│  ⚠️  CRITICAL: selfHeal in production — if an incident response team        │
│      manually scales up a deployment (kubectl scale), selfHeal will         │
│      scale it BACK DOWN. In emergencies, pause ArgoCD first!               │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

ArgoCD Reconciliation Loop — Under the Hood

The application-controller is the brain of ArgoCD. It runs an infinite reconciliation loop that ensures cluster state matches Git state. Understanding this loop is key to debugging sync issues:

ArgoCD Controller Reconciliation Loop (Deep Dive)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ARGOCD APPLICATION CONTROLLER — RECONCILIATION LOOP                         │
│                                                                              │
│  Every 3 minutes (or on webhook):                                            │
│                                                                              │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  PHASE 1: FETCH DESIRED STATE (from Git/Helm repo)                  │    │
│  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │    │
│  │  │ 1. Clone/pull Git repo (shallow clone, --depth=1)          │     │    │
│  │  │ 2. Checkout targetRevision (main branch, tag, or commit)   │     │    │
│  │  │ 3. If Helm: helm template → render YAML                     │     │    │
│  │  │ 4. If Kustomize: kustomize build → render YAML              │     │    │
│  │  │ 5. If plain YAML: read directory as-is                      │     │    │
│  │  │ 6. Result: list of K8s resource objects (desired state)    │     │    │
│  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                    │                                          │
│                                    ▼                                          │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  PHASE 2: FETCH LIVE STATE (from cluster via K8s API)               │    │
│  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │    │
│  │  │ 1. kubectl get <resource> -n <namespace> -o yaml           │     │    │
│  │  │ 2. For each desired resource, fetch live equivalent         │     │    │
│  │  │ 3. Cache live state in Redis for 3 min (reduces API load)  │     │    │
│  │  │ 4. Result: list of K8s resource objects (live state)       │     │    │
│  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                    │                                          │
│                                    ▼                                          │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  PHASE 3: COMPARE (three-way diff)                                   │    │
│  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │    │
│  │  │ 1. Diff desired vs live YAML                                │     │    │
│  │  │ 2. Normalize both sides (strip runtime fields)              │     │    │
│  │  │ 3. Fields normalized out:                                   │     │    │
│  │  │    - metadata.generation, metadata.resourceVersion          │     │    │
│  │  │    - status.* (all status subfields)                        │     │    │
│  │  │    - spec.clusterIP (assigned by cluster)                   │     │    │
│  │  │ 4. Result: Synced (no diff) or OutOfSync (diff found)      │     │    │
│  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                    │                                          │
│                                    ▼                                          │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  PHASE 4: SYNC (if auto-sync or manual trigger)                     │    │
│  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │    │
│  │  │ 1. PreSync hooks execute (kubectl apply hook resources)   │     │    │
│  │  │ 2. Apply resources in wave order (0, 1, 2, ...)           │     │    │
│  │  │ 3. Each resource: kubectl apply -f <resource>              │     │    │
│  │  │ 4. If prune=true: delete resources in live but not in git │     │    │
│  │  │ 5. PostSync hooks execute                                   │     │    │
│  │  │ 6. Health assessment (check pod status, etc.)              │     │    │
│  │  │ 7. Result: Synced + Healthy/Degraded                       │     │    │
│  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                              │
│  ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════     │
│  KEY INSIGHT: ArgoCD uses kubectl apply (declarative), not kubectl create    │
│  (imperative). This means:                                                   │
│  - apply is idempotent — running it twice = same result                     │
│  - apply uses last-applied-configuration annotation to track changes         │
│  - apply can update AND create resources                                     │
│  - Removing a field from Git → apply removes it from cluster               │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

ArgoCD Health Assessment — How Healthy/Degraded Is Determined

ArgoCD doesn't just check if a resource exists — it evaluates resource-specific health rules written in Lua. You can customize these rules for CRDs:

argocd-cm.yaml — Custom health check for Django app CRD 
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: argocd-cm
  namespace: argocd
data:
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # BUILT-IN HEALTH CHECKS (what ArgoCD does internally):
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # Deployment:  Healthy if .status.availableReplicas >= .spec.replicas
  # StatefulSet: Healthy if .status.readyReplicas == .spec.replicas
  # DaemonSet:   Healthy if .status.numberReady == .status.desiredNumberScheduled
  # Service:     Healthy if .spec.type != LoadBalancer OR .status.loadBalancer.ingress exists
  # Ingress:     Healthy if .status.loadBalancer.ingress exists
  # Pod:         Healthy if .status.phase == "Running"
  # Job:         Healthy if .status.succeeded >= 1
  # PersistentVolumeClaim: Healthy if .status.phase == "Bound"

  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # CUSTOM HEALTH CHECK for DjangoApp CRD (Lua script)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  resource.customizations: |
    easypj.io/DjangoApp:
      health.lua: |
        hs = {}
        hs.status = "Progressing"
        hs.message = "Waiting for DjangoApp to be ready"
        
        if obj.status ~= nil then
          if obj.status.phase == "Running" then
            hs.status = "Healthy"
            hs.message = "DjangoApp is running"
            return hs
          elseif obj.status.phase == "Failed" then
            hs.status = "Degraded"
            hs.message = "DjangoApp failed: " .. (obj.status.reason or "unknown")
            return hs
          end
        end
        return hs

Multi-Cluster ArgoCD — Hub-Spoke Pattern

In production, you run ArgoCD in a management cluster and have it deploy to multiple workload clusters. This is the hub-spoke pattern:

Hub-Spoke Architecture

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  MULTI-CLUSTER GITOPS — HUB-SPOKE PATTERN                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                    MANAGEMENT CLUSTER (Hub)                           │   │
│  │                                                                       │   │
│  │  ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────┐         │   │
│  │  │ ArgoCD   │   │ ArgoCD   │   │ Git Repo │   │   SSO    │         │   │
│  │  │ Server   │   │ App Ctlr │   │  Mirror  │   │ (OIDC)   │         │   │
│  │  └──────────┘   └─────┬────┘   └──────────┘   └──────────┘         │   │
│  │                       │                                               │   │
│  └───────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                          │                                                    │
│              ┌───────────┼───────────┐                                       │
│              │           │           │                                        │
│              ▼           ▼           ▼                                        │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐                         │
│  │  PROD-US-EAST │ │  PROD-EU-WEST│ │   STAGING    │   (Spoke Clusters)     │
│  │               │ │               │ │               │                         │
│  │ easypj v2.1   │ │ easypj v2.1   │ │ easypj v2.2   │                         │
│  │ 5 replicas    │ │ 5 replicas    │ │ 2 replicas    │                         │
│  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘                         │
│                                                                              │
│  CONFIGURATION (on hub cluster):                                             │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│  │ # Add spoke clusters to ArgoCD                                     │     │
│  │ $ argocd cluster add prod-us-east-context   # Adds kubeconfig       │     │
│  │ $ argocd cluster add prod-eu-west-context                          │     │
│  │                                                                     │     │
│  │ # Application YAML targets specific cluster:                       │     │
│  │ spec:                                                               │     │
│  │   destination:                                                      │     │
│  │     server: https://prod-us-east-cluster.example.com               │     │
│  │     namespace: easypj                                               │     │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│  BENEFITS:                                                                   │
│  ✅ One ArgoCD instance manages ALL clusters                                 │
│  ✅ Single pane of glass for multi-cluster deployments                       │
│  ✅ Spoke clusters have NO ArgoCD running (less resource usage)              │
│  ✅ If spoke cluster is down, hub still tracks desired state                 │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Diff Customization — Ignoring Irrelevant Differences

Sometimes ArgoCD reports OutOfSync for differences you don't care about (like HPA setting replicas at runtime). Configure diff customization to ignore these:

argocd-cm.yaml — Ignore HPA replicas, mutating webhook annotations 
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: argocd-cm
  namespace: argocd
data:
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # IGNORE FIELDS that change at runtime
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  resource.customizations.ignoreDifferences.all: |
    # Ignore HPA-controlled replica count (HPA changes it dynamically)
    jsonPointers:
    - /spec/replicas
    
  resource.customizations.ignoreDifferences.admissionregistration.k8s.io_MutatingWebhookConfiguration: |
    jsonPointers:
    - /webhooks/0/clientConfig/caBundle    # Rotated by cert-manager
    
  # App-level overrides (in Application YAML):
  # spec:
  #   ignoreDifferences:
  #   - group: apps
  #     kind: Deployment
  #     jsonPointers:
  #     - /spec/replicas                    # Ignore HPA changes

ArgoCD Notifications — Alerting on Sync Failures

ArgoCD can send notifications to Slack, email, or webhooks when syncs succeed, fail, or health degrades:

argocd-notifications-cm.yaml — Slack alerts for easypj 
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: argocd-notifications-cm
  namespace: argocd
data:
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # SLACK INTEGRATION
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  service.slack: |
    token: $slack-token

  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # TRIGGER: When to send notification
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  trigger.on-sync-failed: |
    - when: app.status.operationState.phase == 'Failed'
      send: [on-sync-failed-slack]
  trigger.on-sync-succeeded: |
    - when: app.status.operationState.phase == 'Succeeded'
      send: [on-sync-succeeded-slack]
  trigger.on-health-degraded: |
    - when: app.status.health.status == 'Degraded'
      send: [on-health-degraded-slack]

  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # TEMPLATE: What the message looks like
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  template.on-sync-failed-slack: |
    message: |
      🚨 *Sync FAILED*: {{.app.metadata.name}}
      • Environment: {{.app.spec.destination.namespace}}
      • Revision: {{.app.status.sync.revision}}
      • Error: {{.app.status.operationState.message}}
      • Operator: {{.app.status.operationState.operation.initiatedBy.username}}
      • <{{.context.argocdUrl}}/applications/{{.app.metadata.name}}|View in ArgoCD>

  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # SUBSCRIPTION: Which apps get notified
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  subscriptions: |
    - recipients:
      - slack:easypj-alerts
      triggers:
      - on-sync-failed
      - on-health-degraded
      selector: team=backend    # Only apps with label team=backend

37.3 ArgoCD for easypj — Practical Setup

Here's a complete walkthrough of setting up ArgoCD to deploy easypj using GitOps.

Step 1: Install ArgoCD

Terminal — install ArgoCD 
# Create namespace and install ArgoCD
$ kubectl create namespace argocd
$ kubectl apply -n argocd \
    -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argoproj/argo-cd/stable/manifests/install.yaml

# Wait for all pods to be ready
$ kubectl -n argocd get pods -w
NAME                                  READY   STATUS    RESTARTS
argocd-server-xxxxx                   1/1     Running   0
argocd-repo-server-xxxxx              1/1     Running   0
argocd-application-controller-xxxxx   1/1     Running   0
argocd-redis-xxxxx                    1/1     Running   0

# Get the initial admin password
$ kubectl -n argocd get secret argocd-initial-admin-secret \
    -o jsonpath="{.data.password}" | base64 -d

# Access the UI (port-forward for local access)
$ kubectl port-forward svc/argocd-server -n argocd 8080:443

Step 2: Create ArgoCD Application for easypj

easypj-argocd-app.yaml — ArgoCD Application 
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: easypj
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/youruser/easypj-k8s-manifests
    targetRevision: main          # Track main branch
    path: overlays/production     # Kustomize overlay path
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: easypj
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true                 # Delete resources removed from Git
      selfHeal: true              # Fix manual changes (drift)
    syncOptions:
    - CreateNamespace=true        # Auto-create namespace

easypj GitOps Workflow — Day-to-Day

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  DAILY GITOPS WORKFLOW FOR easypj                                            │
│                                                                              │
│  1. Developer updates easypj code                                            │
│     └── CI builds new image: easypj/web:v2.1                                │
│                                                                              │
│  2. Developer updates manifest repo (PR)                                     │
│     └── Change: image: easypj/web:v2.0 → image: easypj/web:v2.1           │
│                                                                              │
│  3. PR reviewed & merged to main                                           │
│     └── Git log: "Bump easypj to v2.1 — fix login bug"                     │
│                                                                              │
│  4. ArgoCD detects change (3 min polling or webhook)                        │
│     └── Status: OutOfSync → Syncing → Synced ✅                              │
│                                                                              │
│  5. ArgoCD applies changes to cluster                                        │
│     └── Rolling update: v2.0 pods → v2.1 pods                              │
│                                                                              │
│  6. Something wrong? Rollback in seconds!                                    │
│     └── $ git revert HEAD && git push                                     │
│     └── ArgoCD syncs back to v2.0 ✅                                         │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

ArgoCD Troubleshooting — Common Issues

Terminal — ArgoCD debugging commands 
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# CHECK APPLICATION STATUS
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
$ argocd app get easypj
Name:               easypj
Project:            default
Server:             https://kubernetes.default.svc
Namespace:          easypj
Sync Status:        OutOfSync     ← Drift detected!
Health Status:      Degraded       ← Something's wrong

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# SEE WHAT'S DIFFERENT (drift detection)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
$ argocd app diff easypj
===== apps/Deployment easypj/easypj-web ======
  replicas: 3               # Git says 3
- replicas: 5               # Cluster has 5 (someone used kubectl scale!)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# FORCE SYNC (override manual changes)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
$ argocd app sync easypj --force --prune

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# CHECK SYNC HISTORY
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
$ argocd app history easypj
ID  DATE                  REVISION
1   2024-03-10 09:00:00   abc1234 (Deploy v2.0)
2   2024-03-12 14:30:00   def5678 (Fix login bug)
3   2024-03-15 11:00:00   ghi9012 (Scale to 3 replicas)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# ROLLBACK TO PREVIOUS SYNC
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
$ argocd app rollback easypj 2    # Go back to revision 2

ArgoCD Status Cheat Sheet

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ARGOCD STATUS REFERENCE                                                     │
│                                                                              │
│  SYNC STATUS:                                                                │
│  ┌──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ Synced     ✅    │ Cluster matches Git — everything is good         │    │
│  │ OutOfSync  ⚠️    │ Cluster differs from Git — needs sync            │    │
│  │ Unknown    ❓    │ ArgoCD can't determine state                      │    │
│  └──────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                              │
│  HEALTH STATUS:                                                              │
│  ┌──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ Healthy    💚    │ All resources are running correctly               │    │
│  │ Progressing ⏳   │ Resource is updating (rolling update in progress) │    │
│  │ Degraded   🟡    │ Resource is unhealthy (CrashLoop, pending)       │    │
│  │ Suspended  ⏸️    │ Resource is suspended (scaled to 0)              │    │
│  │ Missing    ❌    │ Resource exists in Git but not in cluster         │    │
│  └──────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                              │
│  COMMON TROUBLESHOOTING:                                                     │
│  ┌────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┐        │
│  │ OutOfSync + Healthy        │ Someone used kubectl directly —    │        │
│  │                            │ sync to restore Git state          │        │
│  ├────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤        │
│  │ Synced + Degraded          │ Git state applied but pods         │        │
│  │                            │ crashing — check image/config      │        │
│  ├────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤        │
│  │ OutOfSync + Missing        │ New resource in Git not yet        │        │
│  │                            │ synced — run sync                  │        │
│  ├────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤        │
│  │ Unknown + Unknown          │ ArgoCD can't reach repo or         │        │
│  │                            │ cluster — check credentials        │        │
│  └────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘        │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Sync Waves & Hooks — Controlling Deployment Order

When deploying easypj, order matters: ConfigMap before Deployment, Deployment before HPA, migrate DB before new pods start. Sync waves and hooks let you enforce this:

YAML — Sync waves and hooks for ordered deployment 
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# WAVE 0: Namespace first
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: easypj
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "0"    # Created FIRST

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# WAVE 1: ConfigMaps and Secrets (before pods)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: easypj-config
  namespace: easypj
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1"    # Created SECOND
data:
  DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: "easypj.settings.production"

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# HOOK: PreSync — Run DB migrations before deploy
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: easypj-db-migrate
  namespace: easypj
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync      # Runs BEFORE sync
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy: HookSucceeded  # Clean up after
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: migrate
        image: ghcr.io/youruser/easypj-web:v2.1
        command: ["python", "manage.py", "migrate", "--noinput"]

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# WAVE 2: Deployments (after configs)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: easypj-web
  namespace: easypj
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "2"    # Created THIRD

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# HOOK: PostSync — Run health check (smoke test)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: easypj-smoke-test
  namespace: easypj
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PostSync     # Runs AFTER sync
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy: HookSucceeded
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: test
        image: curlimages/curl:latest
        command: ["sh", "-c"]
        args:
        - |
          # Wait for service, then check health
          sleep 5
          curl -f http://easypj-web.easypj:8000/health/ || exit 1
          echo "✅ easypj is healthy!"

Sync Wave Execution Order

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  SYNC ORDER (single sync operation):                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  Phase 1: PreSync hooks execute                                              │
│  ┌──────────────────┐                                                        │
│  │ DB migration Job  │  → python manage.py migrate                          │
│  └──────┬───────────┘                                                        │
│         │                                                                     │
│  Phase 2: Apply resources in wave order (lowest to highest)                  │
│         ▼                                                                     │
│  Wave 0  Wave 1       Wave 2        Wave 3                                   │
│  ┌────┐  ┌─────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌───────┐                               │
│  │ NS │→│ConfigMap│→│Deployment│→│  HPA  │                               │
│  │    │  │ Secrets │  │ Service  │  │  PDB  │                               │
│  └────┘  └─────────┘  └──────────┘  └───────┘                               │
│                                                                              │
│  Phase 3: PostSync hooks execute                                             │
│  ┌──────────────────┐                                                        │
│  │ Smoke test Job    │  → curl /health/ → ✅ or ❌                           │
│  └──────────────────┘                                                        │
│                                                                              │
│  If PostSync hook FAILS → Sync marked as Failed (but resources stay)        │
│  If PostSync hook SUCCEEDS → Sync = Synced & Healthy                        │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

AppProject — Organizing Multiple Apps with Guardrails

The Application resources live in argocd namespace, but the AppProject defines what destinations and sources are allowed — a crucial security boundary:

easypj-appproject.yaml — Scoped deployment boundaries 
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AppProject
metadata:
  name: easypj-team
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  description: "easypj application project — backend team"

  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # ALLOWED SOURCES — which Git repos / chart repos
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  sourceRepos:
  - https://github.com/youruser/easypj-k8s-manifests
  - https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami   # Allowed Helm charts

  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # ALLOWED DESTINATIONS — which clusters / namespaces
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  destinations:
  - namespace: easypj
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
  - namespace: easypj-staging
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc

  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # ALLOWED RESOURCE KINDS — deny dangerous types
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  clusterResourceWhitelist:
  - group: ""
    kind: Namespace
  - group: "rbac.authorization.k8s.io"
    kind: ClusterRole

  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  # DENY SPECIFIC RESOURCES (blacklist)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════
  namespaceResourceBlacklist:
  - group: ""
    kind: ResourceQuota    # Don't let apps set cluster quotas
  - group: "policy"
    kind: PodSecurityPolicy

⚠️ ArgoCD Gotcha — AppProject vs Application

Every Application must belong to a project (default is project: default). The default project allows ALL sources and ALL destinations — fine for learning, but in production, create scoped AppProjects. If an Application references a repo/destination not whitelisted in its project, ArgoCD shows Unknown status with no helpful error — check the argocd-application-controller logs.

ArgoCD Sync Internals — What Actually Happens During Sync

When ArgoCD syncs, it doesn't just run kubectl apply blindly. It goes through a precise sequence that you can observe and control:

Sync Operation — Phase-by-Phase Breakdown

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  SYNC OPERATION — INTERNAL PHASES                                            │
│                                                                              │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │ PHASE: PreSync (hooks with argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync)            ││
│  │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  ││
│  │ │ • Runs Jobs/Pods marked as PreSync                                 │  ││
│  │ │ • ArgoCD WAITS for these to complete (success or failure)          │  ││
│  │ │ • If PreSync hook FAILS → sync ABORTED (no resources applied)      │  ││
│  │ │ • Use case: DB backup, schema validation, external approval        │  ││
│  │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  ││
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│
│                                    │                                          │
│                                    ▼                                          │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │ PHASE: Sync (apply resources in wave order)                              ││
│  │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  ││
│  │ │ For each wave (0, 1, 2, ...):                                      │  ││
│  │ │   1. kubectl apply --dry-run=client → validate YAML                │  ││
│  │ │   2. If dry-run fails → sync FAILS for that resource               │  ││
│  │ │   3. kubectl apply -f <resource> → actually apply                  │  ││
│  │ │   4. Wait for resource to become "Synced" (matches desired state)  │  ││
│  │ │   5. Move to next resource in same wave (parallel within wave)     │  ││
│  │ │   6. After all resources in wave complete → move to next wave      │  ││
│  │ │                                                                     │  ││
│  │ │ If prune=true:                                                      │  ││
│  │ │   • After ALL waves: delete resources in cluster but NOT in Git    │  ││
│  │ │   • Uses Kubernetes ownerReferences to track what ArgoCD created   │  ││
│  │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  ││
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│
│                                    │                                          │
│                                    ▼                                          │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │ PHASE: PostSync (hooks with argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PostSync)          ││
│  │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  ││
│  │ │ • Runs Jobs/Pods marked as PostSync                                │  ││
│  │ │ • If PostSync FAILS → sync status = "Failed" (but resources stay)  │  ││
│  │ │ • Use case: smoke tests, integration tests, cache warmup           │  ││
│  │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  ││
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│
│                                                                              │
│  ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════     │
│  SYNC OPTIONS (argocd app sync easypj --<option>):                            │
│  ┌─────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ --dry-run       │ Show what WOULD happen (no actual changes)        │    │
│  │ --prune         │ Delete resources not in Git (default with auto)   │    │
│  │ --force         │ Force delete + recreate (for immutable fields)    │    │
│  │ --replace       │ Use kubectl replace instead of apply              │    │
│  │ --server-side   │ Use server-side apply (for large resources)       │    │
│  │ --async         │ Don't wait for sync to complete                   │    │
│  │ --timeout 600   │ Wait up to 600 seconds for sync                   │    │
│  └─────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

ArgoCD Resource Tracking — How ArgoCD Knows What It Manages

ArgoCD adds a special annotation to every resource it creates. This is how it knows which resources to prune and which to ignore:

How ArgoCD tracks managed resources 
# Every resource managed by ArgoCD has this annotation:
$ kubectl get deployment easypj-web -n easypj -o yaml | grep argocd
    argocd.argoproj.io/instance: easypj        # Which Application owns this
    argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id: easypj:apps/Deployment:easypj/easypj-web

# How pruning works:
# 1. ArgoCD lists ALL resources with argocd.argoproj.io/instance=easypj
# 2. Compares this list against what's currently in Git
# 3. Any resource in cluster but NOT in Git → DELETE (if prune=true)
# 4. Any resource in Git but NOT in cluster → CREATE

# This is why you can't "steal" an ArgoCD-managed resource:
# Even if you remove the argocd.argoproj.io/instance annotation,
# selfHeal=true will add it back on the next sync loop!

37.4 Helm — Kubernetes Package Manager

CONCEPT

Helm packages Kubernetes manifests into charts — reusable, versioned, configurable bundles. Think of it as apt or pip for Kubernetes. Values files let you customize the same chart for dev, staging, and production.

Helm Chart Structure — easypj Example

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  HELM CHART DIRECTORY STRUCTURE                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  easypj-chart/                                                               │
│  ├── Chart.yaml              # Chart metadata (name, version, description)  │
│  ├── values.yaml             # Default configuration values                  │
│  ├── values-prod.yaml        # Production overrides                          │
│  ├── templates/                                                              │
│  │   ├── _helpers.tpl        # Template helper functions                     │
│  │   ├── deployment.yaml     # {{ .Values.replicas }}                       │
│  │   ├── service.yaml        # {{ .Values.serviceType }}                    │
│  │   ├── ingress.yaml        # {{ .Values.host }}                           │
│  │   ├── configmap.yaml      # {{ .Values.dbHost }}                         │
│  │   ├── secret.yaml         # {{ .Values.dbPassword }}                     │
│  │   └── hpa.yaml            # {{ .Values.autoscaling.enabled }}            │
│  └── charts/                 # Sub-chart dependencies                        │
│                                                                              │
│  ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════     │
│                                                                              │
│  values.yaml (defaults):       values-prod.yaml (overrides):                │
│  ┌─────────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────────┐                  │
│  │ replicas: 1              │   │ replicas: 3              │                  │
│  │ image:                   │   │ image:                   │                  │
│  │   tag: latest            │   │   tag: v2.1-stable       │                  │
│  │ serviceType: ClusterIP   │   │ serviceType: LoadBalancer│                  │
│  │ resources:               │   │ resources:               │                  │
│  │   requests:              │   │   requests:              │                  │
│  │     cpu: 100m            │   │     cpu: 500m            │                  │
│  │     memory: 128Mi        │   │     memory: 512Mi        │                  │
│  │ ingress:                 │   │ ingress:                 │                  │
│  │   enabled: false         │   │   enabled: true          │                  │
│  │   host: ""               │   │   host: easypj.com      │                  │
│  └─────────────────────────┘   └─────────────────────────┘                  │
│                                                                              │
│  Same chart, different values → different environments! 🎯                  │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Helm Essential Commands

Terminal — Helm workflow 
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# CHART REPOSITORIES
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
$ helm repo add bitnami https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
$ helm repo update
$ helm search repo nginx

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# INSTALL / UPGRADE / ROLLBACK
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# Install easypj chart with production values
$ helm install easypj ./easypj-chart --values values-prod.yaml -n easypj

# Upgrade (change image tag to v2.2)
$ helm upgrade easypj ./easypj-chart --values values-prod.yaml \
    --set image.tag=v2.2 -n easypj

# Oops! Rollback to previous release
$ helm rollback easypj 1 -n easypj

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# INSPECT / DEBUG
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
$ helm list -A                    # List all releases
$ helm history easypj -n easypj   # Release history
$ helm get values easypj -n easypj  # Current values
$ helm template ./easypj-chart    # Render without installing (dry-run)

Helm Go Template Syntax — Crash Course

Helm templates use Go's text/template language. Here's how a real Helm deployment template looks for easypj:

templates/deployment.yaml — Helm Go template syntax 
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  # {{ .Release.Name }} = helm install NAME → "easypj"
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-web
  labels:
    {{- include "easypj.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicas | default 1 }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: {{ .Release.Name }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: {{ .Release.Name }}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
        image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
        ports:
        - containerPort: {{ .Values.containerPort | default 8000 }}
        {{- if .Values.resources }}
        resources:
          {{- toYaml .Values.resources | nindent 10 }}
        {{- end }}
        {{- if .Values.env }}
        env:
        {{- range .Values.env }}
        - name: {{ .name }}
          value: {{ .value | quote }}
        {{- end }}
        {{- end }}
      {{- if .Values.nodeSelector }}
      nodeSelector:
        {{- toYaml .Values.nodeSelector | nindent 8 }}
      {{- end }}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# GO TEMPLATE CHEAT SHEET:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# {{ .Values.xxx }}           → Read from values.yaml
# {{ .Release.Name }}         → Helm release name
# {{ .Chart.Name }}           → From Chart.yaml
# {{ .Release.Namespace }}    → Target namespace
# {{- ... }}                  → Trim left whitespace
# {{ ... -}}                  → Trim right whitespace
# {{ if .Values.x }}...{{ end }}  → Conditional
# {{ range .Values.list }}        → Loop
# {{ include "tpl" . }}           → Include named template
# {{ toYaml .Values.x | nindent 4 }} → Render as YAML
# {{ .Values.x | default "val" }}     → Default value
# {{ .Values.x | quote }}        → Wrap in quotes
⚠️ Helm Debugging Tips

Template not rendering correctly? Use helm template ./chart --debug to see the rendered YAML. Common errors: missing {{- }} whitespace control causes extra blank lines, and forgetting | nindent N causes YAML indentation errors. Always validate with helm lint ./chart before installing.

Helm Chart Dependencies — Composing the Stack

Helm charts can depend on other charts. For easypj to run, it needs PostgreSQL and Redis. Instead of creating them manually, declare them as dependencies:

Chart.yaml — easypj with sub-chart dependencies 
apiVersion: v2
name: easypj
description: A Helm chart for easypj Django application
type: application
version: 1.0.0
appVersion: "2.1.0"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# CHART DEPENDENCIES (installed automatically)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
dependencies:
- name: postgresql
  version: "15.x.x"
  repository: https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
  condition: postgresql.enabled      # Can toggle via --set postgresql.enabled=false
  alias: easypj-db                   # Referenced as .Values.easypj-db in templates

- name: redis
  version: "19.x.x"
  repository: https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
  condition: redis.enabled
  alias: easypj-cache

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# DOWNLOAD DEPENDENCIES
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# $ helm dependency update    # Downloads charts/ directory
# $ helm dependency build     # Builds from Chart.lock
💡 Dependency Benefits for CKA Context

When you helm install easypj ./chart, Helm automatically installs PostgreSQL and Redis first, then easypj. This mirrors what Kubernetes operators do — one command stands up an entire multi-tier application. The CKA may test your ability to troubleshoot multi-tier deployments, where knowing dependency order (DB before app) saves time diagnosing CrashLoopBackOff.

Helm Hooks — Controlling Install/Upgrade Lifecycle

Just like ArgoCD hooks, Helm hooks run Jobs at specific lifecycle stages. Common use: run Django database migrations before the new deployment starts:

templates/hook-db-migrate.yaml — Helm pre-upgrade hook 
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-db-migrate
  annotations:
    # Run BEFORE upgrade (migrate DB, then start new pods)
    "helm.sh/hook": pre-upgrade
    # Delete job after it succeeds (no clutter)
    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": hook-succeeded
    # Job must complete before deployment rolls out
    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "0"
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: migrate
        image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
        command: ["python", "manage.py", "migrate", "--noinput"]

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# HELM HOOK REFERENCE:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# pre-install      → Before chart is first installed
# post-install     → After chart is first installed
# pre-delete       → Before resources are deleted
# post-delete      → After resources are deleted
# pre-upgrade      → Before an upgrade (release exists)
# post-upgrade     → After an upgrade
# pre-rollback     → Before a rollback
# post-rollback    → After a rollback
# test             → When `helm test` is run

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# HOOK DELETE POLICIES:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# hook-succeeded   → Delete after success (cleanup)
# hook-failed      → Delete after failure (leave for debugging)
# before-hook-creation → Delete previous hook before running again

Helm Test — Verifying a Release

Helm supports built-in test pods that validate a deployment is working. The test runs in its own pod and reports success/failure without affecting production traffic:

templates/tests/test-health.yaml — Automated smoke test 
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: "{{ .Release.Name }}-health-test"
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/hook": test        # Only runs during `helm test`
    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": hook-succeeded
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: curlimages/curl:latest
    command: ["sh", "-c"]
    args:
    - |
      STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
        http://{{ .Release.Name }}-web.{{ .Release.Namespace }}:8000/health/)
      if [ "$STATUS" != "200" ]; then
        echo "❌ Health check failed: HTTP $STATUS"
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "✅ easypj is healthy (HTTP $STATUS)"

# Usage:
# $ helm install easypj ./chart
# $ helm test easypj              # Run the test pod
# NAME: easypj-health-test
# STATUS: Succeeded
# ✅ easypj is healthy (HTTP 200)

Helm Release Storage — Where Helm Keeps State

Helm doesn't have a database. It stores release history as Kubernetes Secrets (or ConfigMaps in Helm 2). Every install, upgrade, or rollback creates a new versioned Secret:

Helm Release Storage Internals

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  HELM RELEASE STORAGE — VERSIONED SECRETS                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  $ helm install easypj ./chart -n easypj                                     │
│  → Creates Secret: sh.helm.release.v1.easypj.v1                              │
│                                                                              │
│  $ helm upgrade easypj ./chart --set replicas=3 -n easypj                    │
│  → Creates Secret: sh.helm.release.v1.easypj.v2                              │
│                                                                              │
│  $ helm upgrade easypj ./chart --set image.tag=v2.2 -n easypj                │
│  → Creates Secret: sh.helm.release.v1.easypj.v3                              │
│                                                                              │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
│  │ $ kubectl get secrets -n easypj -l owner=helm                   │        │
│  │ NAME                               TYPE     DATA   AGE            │        │
│  │ sh.helm.release.v1.easypj.v1       helm.sh/release.v1   1   2d   │        │
│  │ sh.helm.release.v1.easypj.v2       helm.sh/release.v1   1   1d   │        │
│  │ sh.helm.release.v1.easypj.v3       helm.sh/release.v1   1   2h   │        │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
│                                                                              │
│  WHAT'S INSIDE EACH SECRET:                                                  │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
│  │ $ helm get manifest easypj --revision 2                         │        │
│  │ # Shows the EXACT YAML that was applied at revision 2           │        │
│  │                                                                  │        │
│  │ $ helm get values easypj --revision 2                            │        │
│  │ # Shows the values used at revision 2                            │        │
│  │                                                                  │        │
│  │ $ helm get hooks easypj --revision 2                             │        │
│  │ # Shows any hooks that ran at revision 2                         │        │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
│                                                                              │
│  ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════     │
│                                                                              │
│  RELEASE STORAGE LIMITS:                                                     │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
│  │ • Default: keeps last 256 revisions (configurable with          │        │
│  │   --history-max flag)                                            │        │
│  │ • Each secret is ~10KB (base64+gzip encoded manifest)           │        │
│  │ • 256 revisions × ~10KB = ~2.5MB per release                    │        │
│  │ • 100 releases × 2.5MB = 250MB of cluster storage               │        │
│  │ • Tip: $ helm upgrade --history-max 10  # Keep only 10 revs     │        │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
│                                                                              │
│  ⚠️  CRITICAL: Helm 3 uses Secrets (base64, not encrypted). Anyone with     │
│      kubectl get secrets access can read ALL your Helm values including     │
│      passwords! Use sealed-secrets or external-secrets for sensitive data.  │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Helm Rendering Pipeline — From Chart to YAML Step-by-Step

Understanding the exact sequence Helm follows when rendering templates is essential for debugging. Here's the complete pipeline:

The Helm Template Rendering Pipeline

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  HELM RENDERING PIPELINE (what `helm template` does internally)              │
│                                                                              │
│  INPUT:                                                                       │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
│  │ 1. values.yaml (default values)                                   │       │
│  │ 2. --values values-prod.yaml (user overrides)                     │       │
│  │ 3. --set replicas=5 (command-line overrides, HIGHEST priority)    │       │
│  │ 4. Chart.yaml (metadata about this chart)                         │       │
│  │ 5. templates/*.yaml (Go template files)                           │       │
│  │ 6. charts/* (dependency charts, if any)                           │       │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘       │
│                                    │                                          │
│                                    ▼                                          │
│  STEP 1: VALUE MERGING (from lowest to highest priority)                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
│  │ Priority (lowest → highest):                                      │       │
│  │   values.yaml  →  parent chart values  →  --values file          │       │
│  │   → --set key=val  →  --set-string key=val                       │       │
│  │                                                                    │       │
│  │ Example:                                                          │       │
│  │   values.yaml:        replicas: 1                                 │       │
│  │   values-prod.yaml:   replicas: 3                                 │       │
│  │   --set replicas=5                                                │       │
│  │   → Final: replicas = 5 (--set wins)                             │       │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘       │
│                                    │                                          │
│                                    ▼                                          │
│  STEP 2: BUILD RENDER CONTEXT (the "." object)                                │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
│  │ The "." passed to templates contains:                             │       │
│  │                                                                    │       │
│  │ .Values          → merged values from step 1                      │       │
│  │ .Release          → release metadata:                             │       │
│  │   .Name           → "easypj" (helm install NAME)                  │       │
│  │   .Namespace      → "easypj" (-n flag)                            │       │
│  │   .Revision       → 1, 2, 3, ... (auto-incrementing)             │       │
│  │   .IsInstall      → true on first install                         │       │
│  │   .IsUpgrade       → true on upgrades                             │       │
│  │ .Chart            → Chart.yaml contents                           │       │
│  │   .Name            → "easypj"                                     │       │
│  │   .Version         → "1.0.0"                                      │       │
│  │   .AppVersion      → "2.1.0"                                      │       │
│  │ .Capabilities      → K8s cluster capabilities:                   │       │
│  │   .KubeVersion     → "1.30" (server version)                      │       │
│  │   .APIVersions     → all available API versions                   │       │
│  │ .Template          → current template info                        │       │
│  │   .Name            → "easypj/templates/deployment.yaml"           │       │
│  │   .BasePath        → path to templates/ directory                 │       │
│  │ .Files             → access to non-template files in chart/       │       │
│  │ .Library           → library chart utilities                      │       │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘       │
│                                    │                                          │
│                                    ▼                                          │
│  STEP 3: TEMPLATE EXECUTION (for each file in templates/)                    │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
│  │ For each file in templates/ (NOT in templates/NOTES.txt):         │       │
│  │                                                                    │       │
│  │ a. Parse file as Go text/template                                 │       │
│  │ b. Execute template with merged context "."                        │       │
│  │ c. Apply Sprig template functions (60+ functions)                  │       │
│  │ d. Collect output (rendered YAML string)                           │       │
│  │                                                                    │       │
│  │ Special files:                                                    │       │
│  │   templates/NOTES.txt → rendered AFTER install (helm status)      │       │
│  │   templates/tests/    → only executed during `helm test`          │       │
│  │   templates/_*.tpl    → partials, NOT rendered directly           │       │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘       │
│                                    │                                          │
│                                    ▼                                          │
│  STEP 4: YAML PARSING & VALIDATION                                           │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
│  │ a. Split multi-document YAML (--- separator)                      │       │
│  │ b. Parse each document as K8s resource                            │       │
│  │ c. Validate required fields: apiVersion, kind, metadata.name      │       │
│  │ d. If validation fails → ERROR (with template file + line)        │       │
│  │ e. helm lint does extra: checks for deprecated APIs               │       │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘       │
│                                    │                                          │
│                                    ▼                                          │
│  STEP 5: RESOURCE ORDERING (for apply)                                       │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
│  │ Helm applies resources in this order (Helm's built-in sort):      │       │
│  │                                                                    │       │
│  │ 1. Namespace        6. Deployment                                 │       │
│  │ 2. NetworkPolicy     7. StatefulSet                               │       │
│  │ 3. ResourceQuota     8. DaemonSet                                 │       │
│  │ 4. LimitRange        9. Job                                       │       │
│  │ 5. PodSecurityPolicy 10. CronJob                                  │       │
│  │ 11. Secret/ConfigMap 12. Service                                  │       │
│  │ 13. Ingress          14. PVC                                      │       │
│  │ 15. ServiceAccount   16. Role/RoleBinding                         │       │
│  │ 17. ClusterRole/CRB  18. Hooks run at specific lifecycle points   │       │
│  │                                                                    │       │
│  │ ⚠️  Helm's built-in ordering is NOT always correct for your app. │       │
│  │     Use hook weights (helm.sh/hook-weight: "0") to control order. │       │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘       │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Chart.lock — Reproducible Deployments

Just like package-lock.json or go.sum, Helm's Chart.lock pins exact dependency versions for reproducible builds:

Chart.lock — Pinned dependency versions 
dependencies:
- name: postgresql
  repository: https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
  version: 15.5.20          # EXACT version (from Chart.yaml: "15.x.x")
- name: redis
  repository: https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
  version: 19.6.2            # EXACT version (from Chart.yaml: "19.x.x")
digest: sha256:8f9e7d6c5b4a3e2d1f0e9d8c7b6a5f4e3d2c1b0a9e8f7d6c5b4a3e2d1f0e9

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# Why Chart.lock matters:
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# Without lock: helm dependency update may fetch 15.5.21 (patch bump)
#                → Could introduce bugs from dependency change
# With lock:    helm dependency build uses EXACT versions from lock
#                → Reproducible across CI, dev laptops, production
#
# Rule: COMMIT Chart.lock to Git. It's generated code but critical
#       for reproducibility. CI should fail if lock is out of date.

37.5 Kustomize — Built-in Manifest Customization

CONCEPT

Kustomize is built into kubectl — no separate binary needed. It uses a base + overlays pattern: write your YAML once (base), and patch it per environment (overlays). No templates, no Go syntax — just strategic merge patches on plain YAML.

Kustomize Directory Structure — easypj

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  KUSTOMIZE BASE + OVERLAYS PATTERN                                          │
│                                                                              │
│  easypj-kustomize/                                                           │
│  ├── base/                          # Shared across ALL environments         │
│  │   ├── kustomization.yaml         # Lists resources to include             │
│  │   ├── deployment.yaml            # easypj base: replicas: 1              │
│  │   ├── service.yaml               # ClusterIP service                     │
│  │   └── configmap.yaml             # Shared config values                  │
│  │                                                                           │
│  └── overlays/                      # Per-environment patches                │
│      ├── dev/                                                                │
│      │   ├── kustomization.yaml     # bases: [../../base]                   │
│      │   └── patch-replicas.yaml    # replicas: 1, cpu: 100m               │
│      │                                                                       │
│      ├── staging/                                                            │
│      │   ├── kustomization.yaml     # bases: [../../base]                   │
│      │   └── patch-resources.yaml   # replicas: 2, cpu: 250m               │
│      │                                                                       │
│      └── production/                                                         │
│          ├── kustomization.yaml     # bases: [../../base]                   │
│          ├── patch-replicas.yaml    # replicas: 5                           │
│          └── patch-resources.yaml   # cpu: 500m, memory: 512Mi             │
│                                                                              │
│  ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════     │
│                                                                              │
│  Deploy:   $ kubectl apply -k overlays/production/                           │
│  Preview:  $ kubectl kustomize overlays/production/                          │
│                                                                              │
│  Result: base/deployment.yaml MERGED with production patches                 │
│  → replicas: 5, cpu: 500m, memory: 512Mi                                    │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Kustomize Files for easypj

base/kustomization.yaml & overlays/production/kustomization.yaml 
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# base/kustomization.yaml
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
- deployment.yaml
- service.yaml
- configmap.yaml
commonLabels:
  app: easypj

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# overlays/production/kustomization.yaml
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
- ../../base
namePrefix: prod-              # All resources get prod- prefix
namespace: easypj-production
patches:
- path: patch-replicas.yaml
  target:
    kind: Deployment
    name: easypj-web
images:
- name: easypj/web
  newTag: v2.1-stable          # Override image tag for prod

---
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# overlays/production/patch-replicas.yaml
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: easypj-web
spec:
  replicas: 5                  # Production: 5 replicas
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: easypj
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "1000m"
            memory: "1Gi"

Kustomize Power Features — Generators & Transformers

kustomization.yaml — Generators, labels, and config management 
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
- ../../base

namespace: easypj-production

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# CONFIGMAP GENERATOR — auto-creates ConfigMaps from files/literals
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
configMapGenerator:
- name: easypj-config
  literals:
  - DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=easypj.settings.production
  - ALLOWED_HOSTS=easypj.com
  - DEBUG=false

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# SECRET GENERATOR — auto-creates Secrets
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
secretGenerator:
- name: easypj-db-creds
  literals:
  - DB_PASSWORD=supersecret   # In real life: use sealed-secrets or external-secrets
  type: Opaque

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# COMMON LABELS — applied to ALL resources
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
commonLabels:
  app: easypj
  env: production
  team: backend

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# COMMON ANNOTATIONS
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
commonAnnotations:
  managed-by: kustomize

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# IMAGE TRANSFORMER — override image tags
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
images:
- name: easypj/web
  newName: ghcr.io/youruser/easypj-web
  newTag: v2.1-stable

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# PATCHES — strategic merge or JSON patches
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
patches:
- path: patch-replicas.yaml
  target:
    kind: Deployment
    name: easypj-web
🏋️ Practice Drill — Kustomize Multi-Environment Deploy

Scenario: Deploy easypj to staging and production using Kustomize overlays with different configurations.

  1. Preview what Kustomize will generate for production:
    kubectl kustomize overlays/production/
  2. Apply the production overlay:
    kubectl apply -k overlays/production/
  3. Verify resources were created in the correct namespace:
    kubectl get all -n easypj-production
  4. Check that labels were applied correctly:
    kubectl get deploy -n easypj-production --show-labels
  5. Verify the image tag matches the overlay:
    kubectl get deploy easypj-web -n easypj-production -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
  6. Compare with staging config:
    diff <(kubectl kustomize overlays/staging/) <(kubectl kustomize overlays/production/)

Key point: Same base YAML, but -k flag applies environment-specific patches. This is DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) for Kubernetes!

🎯 CKA Exam — Kustomize

The CKA exam may reference Kustomize in the exam environment. Know these two commands cold: kubectl apply -k <directory> applies Kustomize configuration, and kubectl kustomize <directory> previews without applying. The -k flag is your friend!

Replacements — Cross-Resource Value Injection (Substitutions)

Kustomize replacements (replacing the deprecated vars) let you inject values from one resource into another — like taking a Service's ClusterIP and putting it into a ConfigMap:

kustomization.yaml — Replacements for cross-resource references 
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# USE CASE: Inject Service name into Django ALLOWED_HOSTS
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
- ../../base

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# REPLACEMENT: Take Service name → inject into ConfigMap
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
replacements:
- source:
    kind: Service
    name: easypj-web
    fieldPath: metadata.name        # Source: "prod-easypj-web"
  targets:
  - select:
      kind: ConfigMap
      name: easypj-config
    fieldPaths:
    - data.ANIHU_SERVICE_NAME       # Target: ANIHU_SERVICE_NAME=prod-easypj-web

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# RESULT (rendered output):
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# apiVersion: v1
# kind: ConfigMap
# metadata:
#   name: easypj-config
# data:
#   ANIHU_SERVICE_NAME: prod-easypj-web    ← Injected from Service!

# ═══════════════════════════════════════
# ANOTHER EXAMPLE: Inject namespace into deployment env
# ═══════════════════════════════════════
replacements:
- source:
    kind: Namespace
    name: easypj-production
    fieldPath: metadata.name
  targets:
  - select:
      kind: Deployment
      name: easypj-web
    fieldPaths:
    - spec.template.spec.containers.[name=easypj].env.[name=K8S_NAMESPACE].value

Patch Types — Strategic Merge vs JSON Patch (6902)

Kustomize supports two patch strategies. Know when to use each:

Strategic Merge vs JSON Patch — Comparison

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PATCH TYPE COMPARISON                                                        │
│                                                                              │
│  STRATEGIC MERGE PATCH (default for patches:):                               │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
│  │ File: patch-replicas.yaml                                       │        │
│  │ apiVersion: apps/v1                                              │        │
│  │ kind: Deployment                                                 │        │
│  │ metadata:                                                        │        │
│  │   name: easypj-web                                              │        │
│  │ spec:                                                            │        │
│  │   replicas: 5         ← Merged: ONLY this field changes         │        │
│  │                                                                  │        │
│  │ ✅ K8s-aware: knows list merge strategy for containers, ports   │        │
│  │ ✅ Simple: just write the YAML you want to override             │        │
